A. General

22-00-00-500-801MMEL 22-5 (DDPG) Preparation - Mach Trim Systems Inoperative ATA 22 · Task 500-801

Task Description

4. MMEL 22-5 (DDPG) Preparation - Mach Trim Systems Inoperative

A. General

(1) This task contains the maintenance procedure that prepares the airplane for flight when one or both of the Mach Trim Systems are inoperative.

B. References

Reference Title 22-11-00-740-806 BITE Library Test (P/B 501) 24-22-00-860-811 Supply Electrical Power (P/B 201) 29-11-00-860-801 Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization (P/B 201) 29-11-00-860-805 Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal (P/B 201)

C. Location Zones

Zone Area 210 Subzone - Control Compartment - Body Station 178.00 to Body Station 259.50 22-00-00

D. Single Mach Trim System Deactivation

SUBTASK 22-00-00-860-003 (1) Do these steps to make sure that the remaining Mach Trim System and MACH TRIM FAIL light operate normally: (a) If channel A fails, open these circuit breakers and install safety locks: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name C 4 C00456 AFCS SYS A MACH TRIM AC D 4 C00457 AFCS SYS A MACH TRIM DC (b) If channel B fails, open these circuit breakers and install safety locks: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name B 2 C01064 AFCS SYS B MACH TRIM DC C 1 C01037 AFCS SYS B MACH TRIM AC (c) Make sure that electrical power is supplied (TASK 24-22-00-860-811). (d) If channel A fails, do the DFCS library test No. 33, Mach Trim, for channel B, do this task: BITE Library Test, TASK 22-11-00-740-806. 1) Make sure that the test passes. (e) If channel B fails, do the DFCS library test No. 33, Mach Trim, for channel A, do this task: BITE Library Test, TASK 22-11-00-740-806. 1) Make sure that the test passes.

E. Dual Mach Trim System Deactivation

SUBTASK 22-00-00-860-001 (1) Do these steps to deactivate the mach trim systems: WARNING KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT AWAY FROM THE FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES. THE AILERONS, THE ELEVATORS, THE RUDDER, THE FLAPS, THE SLATS, THE SPOILERS, THE STABILIZER AND THE NOSE GEAR CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (a) Supply hydraulic power to hydraulic systems A and B, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801. (b) Make sure that the flaps are set to 0. (c) Put the stabilizer to 4 units of trim. (d) Move the control column slightly to put the elevators in the detent position. (e) Make sure that the elevator trailing edge is aligned with the elevator index mark on the tailcone at 0.00 ±0.06 in. (0.0 ±1.5 mm). NOTE: If the elevator trailing edge is out of alignment, a Mach Trim Actuator and Mach Trim System are required to position it. An actuator or accessory box that does not operate must be replaced. NOTE: If the elevator trailing edge is not aligned with the index mark on the fuselage, dispatch with both Mach Trim Systems inoperative is not allowed. 22-00-00 (f) Open these circuit breakers and install safety locks: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name C 4 C00456 AFCS SYS A MACH TRIM AC D 4 C00457 AFCS SYS A MACH TRIM DC F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name B 2 C01064 AFCS SYS B MACH TRIM DC C 1 C01037 AFCS SYS B MACH TRIM AC (g) Remove hydraulic power from hydraulic systems A and B, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805.

SUBTASK 22-00-00-860-002 (1) Remove the safety locks and close these circuit breakers: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name C 4 C00456 AFCS SYS A MACH TRIM AC D 4 C00457 AFCS SYS A MACH TRIM DC F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name B 2 C01064 AFCS SYS B MACH TRIM DC C 1 C01037 AFCS SYS B MACH TRIM AC SUBTASK 22-00-00-740-001 (2) Do these steps to do a test of the mach trim system: 22-00-00 (a) From the INIT/REF INDEX screen on the CDU, make these selections: 1) MAINT> 2) <DFCS 3) <FAULT REVIEW 4) <CURRENT STATUS 5) Do steps as required on CDU screen. 6) <CONTINUE (b) If the CURRENT STATUS test fails, correct the fault shown on the CDU. (d) Make these selections on the CDU: 1) <CHANNEL A AND B 2) <MACH TRIM SYSTEM 3) Do steps as required on CDU screen. 4) <CONTINUE (e) If the surface test passes, then there was an intermittent fault. 22-11-00-700-801Land Verify Test ATA 22 · Task 700-801

Task Description

2. Land Verify Test

A. General

(1) The Land Verify Test does a check on the interfaces between the Digital Flight Control System (DFCS) and its Line Replaceable Unit (LRU). (2) The Land Verify Test contains a quick test (autotest), an interactive test and a surface test. (a) The sequence of the Land Verify Test is as follows: 1) Autotests 2) Interactive Tests 3) Surface Tests (b) The autotests are automatic. (c) The interactive tests are not automatic. You must do the instructions that show on the Control Display Unit (CDU) display to complete the interactive tests. (d) The surface tests are not automatic and hydraulic power is necessary for the surface tests. You must do the instructions that show on the CDU display to complete the surface tests. 22-11-00-740-801Digital Flight Control System (DFCS) - Operational Test ATA 22 · Task 740-801

Task Description

2. Digital Flight Control System (DFCS) - Operational Test

A. General

(1) The Digital Flight Control System (DFCS) operational test does a quick check of the serviceable condition of the DFCS. It uses no external equipment. Electrical power and hydraulic power are the only power sources that are necessary for this test. (2) Do the DFCS operational test from the Control Display Unit (CDU). The first test is a check of the Flight Control Computer (FCC) software part number. Then use the current status quick test and five additional tests under the CURRENT STATUS item on the DFCS BITE TEST Fault Review menu. (3) The CURRENT STATUS item on the DFCS BITE TEST FAULT REVIEW menu contains these tests: (a) Current Status Quick Test (Group 10) (b) Additional Tests: 1) Autopilot (Group 11) 2) Flight Director (Group 12) 3) Mach Trim System (Group 13) 4) Speed Trim System (Group 14) 22-11-00 RYR 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020 5) Stab/Speed Trim System (Group 14) RYR ALL 6) Altitude Alert (Group 15) (c) The current status quick test comes before the additional tests. In each additional test, if there are interactive and surface tests, then the interactive tests come before the surface tests. The sequence of the Current Status test is as follows: 1) Current Status Quick Test 2) Additional test a) Interactive tests b) Surface tests (4) The current status quick test contains a number of library tests. NOTE: These library tests are automatic and they are referred to as autotests. (5) There are five additional tests. NOTE: Each additional test contains a number of library tests. These library tests are interactive and/or surface tests. (a) The interactive tests are not automatic. NOTE: You must do the instructions that show on the CDU display to complete the interactive tests. (b) The surface tests are not automatic and hydraulic power is necessary for the surface tests. NOTE: You must do the instructions that show on the CDU display to complete the surface tests. SUBTASK 22-11-00-420-001 (1) Do these steps to test the software part number: (a) If you are not at one of the DFCS BITE TEST displays, do these steps: 1) Push the INIT REF key on the CDU keyboard. 2) If the POS INIT display shows, push the Line Select Key (LSK) adjacent to INDEX. NOTE: This makes the INIT/REF INDEX show. 3) Push the LSK adjacent to MAINT . (b) From the MAINT BITE INDEX, push the LSK adjacent to DFCS. NOTE: The DFCS will do a self-test. 22-11-00 (c) When the self-test is complete, push the LSK adjacent to IDENTIFICATION AND CONFIGURATION. NOTE: The software part number shows below FCC Operational Program Software (OPS). (e) Push the LSK adjacent to PREV MENU. (f) Push the LSK adjacent to CHANNEL B. 1) Make sure that the software part number for Flight Control Computer B (FCC-B) is correct. NOTE: The software part number shows below FCC OPS. F. Current Status Tests SUBTASK 22-11-00-740-001 (1) Push the INIT REF key on the CDU keyboard. (a) Push the LSK that is adjacent to each selection: NOTE: If the CONTINUE shows during the BITE test, do the instructions that show on the CDU display before you push the LSK that is adjacent to CONTINUE. Use the NEXT PAGE or PREV PAGE key to change page if it is necessary. 1) INDEX 2) MAINT 3) DFCS 4) FAULT REVIEW 5) CURRENT STATUS 6) Select channel A, B, or A and B. (b) Autotest: 1) Do the instructions that show on the CDU display. NOTE: If the initialization setup is correct, AUTOTEST IN PROGRESS will show on the CDU display. 2) If AUTOTEST PASSED shows on the CDU display, the test is completed with no failure. NOTE: Some autotests can be completed very fast and you cannot see the AUTOTEST PASSED message. The autotest passed if the AUTOTEST FAILED message is not seen. NOTE: When all the autotests are completed, the summary page shows AUTOTEST PASSED or AUTOTEST FAILED. 3) If AUTOTEST FAILED shows, do the library test(s) that shows on the CDU display. 22-11-00 4) Make a record of the channel (A, B, or A/B), suspect Line Replaceable Unit (LRU)s and the pin numbers that show on the CDU display. NOTE: You can find the channel data adjacent to the INPUT/OUTPUT PINS that shows on the CDU display. Channel A is for the FCC-A and channel B is for the FCC-B. If there is no pin number for the suspect LRU, the channel data does not show. NOTE: Each suspect LRU is referred to as a maintenance message. a) If it is necessary to do the test again, do these steps: b) Push the LSK adjacent to TEST DATA. c) Push the LSK adjacent to RERUN. 5) Refer to 22-Maintenance Message Index in the FIM to find the fault isolation task for the applicable maintenance message. (c) Additional Test: NOTE: The additional test comes immediately after you complete the last autotest. 1) Push the LSK that is adjacent to the additional test. NOTE: When the test is completed and to make the selection for the next additional test, you can push the LSK adjacent to PREV MENU until you see the CURRENT STATUS SELECT ADDITIONAL TEST menu again. a) Make sure that the autopilot, flight director, mach trim system, speed trim system, and alt alert tests are done. 2) AUTOPILOT a) Do the interactive tests. b) Do the surface tests. c) Make sure that the Autopilot Test is completed with no failure. 3) FLIGHT DIRECTOR a) Do the interactive tests. b) Do the surface test. 22-11-00-740-806BITE Library Test ATA 22 · Task 740-806

Task Description

5. BITE Library Test

A. General

(1) The BITE library Test does a check on the interfaces between the Digital Flight Control System (DFCS) and its Line Replaceable Unit (LRU)s. (2) The BITE Library Test contains three types of tests. The quick test (autotest), interactive test and surface test. The autotest comes before the interactive test, and the interactive test comes before the surface test. (a) The sequence of the BITE Library Test is as follows: 1) Autotests 2) Interactive Tests 3) Surface Tests (b) The autotests are automatic. (c) The interactive tests are not automatic. You must do the instructions that show on the Control Display Unit (CDU) display to complete the interactive tests. (d) The surface tests are not automatic and hydraulic power is necessary for the surface tests. You must do the instructions that show on the CDU display to complete the surface tests. 22-11-00 (3) Autotests Table 510/22-11-00-993-815 Library Test Name Group No./ Library Test No. ADIRU 60.01 Autothrottle 60.04 DME 60.05 LRRA 60.07 LNAV 60.11*[1] MCP INTERF 60.16 FMC 60.18 Analog Sensors 60.21 SMYDC 60.22 VOR 60.23 MMR/ILS 60.24 CDS 60.25 MCP Display/Selftest 60.57 Discrete Input 60.70 *[1] Library test 60.11 is available for airplanes with Honeywell Flight Control Computer (FCC)s and with these program pins: • For Flight Control Computer A (FCC-A): D10135A –A05/G05 both open or D10135A –A05 is open and D10135A –G05 is ground • For FCC-A: D10137A –A05/G05 both open or D10137A –A05 is open and D10137A –G05 is ground. (4) Interactive Tests Table 511/22-11-00-993-816 Library Test Name Group No./ Library Test No. ADIRU 60.01 VOR 60.23 MMR/ILS *[1] 60.24 MCP Pushbuttons 60.50 MCP F/D Switches 60.51 MCP IAS/Mach Changeover 60.52 MCP Bank Angle Limit 60.53 MCP Speed Select 60.54 MCP Altitude Select Knob 60.55 MCP Vertical Speed Knob 60.56 MCP Displays/Selftest 60.57 22-11-00 Table 511/22-11-00-993-816 (Continued) Library Test Name Group No./ Library Test No. MCP CMD/CWS Interlock 60.58 MCP Course/Heading Select 60.59 ALT Alert 60.61 Disengage Warning 60.62 *[1] NOTE: If the airplane has a heads-up guidance system (HGS) installed and is powered ON, make sure that the HGS is not operating in primary (PRI) or autoland (AIII) mode before performing the interactive test 60.24, otherwise the test can fail. (5) Surface Tests Table 512/22-11-00-993-817 Library Test Name Group No./ Library Test No. Elevator 60.30 Aileron 60.31 Speed/Stab Trim 60.32 Mach Trim 60.33 Flaps 60.34 Dual Stab 60.35

NOTE: If the system continues to fail with expanded limits, it is necessary to check the friction in the elevator cable system, including all pulleys. Also it is necessary to check the spring force of the springs within the feel of centering (TASK 27-31-64-400-802). NOTE: You can find the channel data adjacent to the INPUT/OUTPUT PINS that shows on the CDU display. Channel A is for the FCC-A and channel B is for the Flight Control Computer B (FCC-B). NOTE: Each suspect LRU is referred to as a maintenance message. a) If it is necessary to do the test again, do these steps: b) Push the LSK adjacent to TEST DATA. c) Push the LSK adjacent to RERUN. 5) Refer to 22-Maintenance Message Index in the FIM to find the fault isolation task for the applicable maintenance message. (c) Interactive Test: NOTE: The interactive tests come immediately after you complete the last autotest. 1) Do the instructions that show on the CDU display to complete all the interactive tests. 22-11-00-740-810Circuit Breaker Interface Test ATA 22 · Task 740-810

Task Description

9. Circuit Breaker Interface Test

A. General

(1) The Circuit Breaker Interface Test does a check on the interfaces between the Digital Flight Control System (DFCS) and all of its circuit breakers.

B. References

Reference Title 24-22-00-860-811 Supply Electrical Power (P/B 201) 24-22-00-860-812 Remove Electrical Power (P/B 201) 29-11-00-860-805 Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal (P/B 201)

SUBTASK 22-11-00-860-088 (4) Make sure that the VHF NAV and IRS switches, on the P5 forward overhead panel, are in the NORMAL positions. SUBTASK 22-11-00-860-089 (5) Set the left and right IRS select switches, on the P5 aft overhead panel, to the ALIGN or NAV position.

E. Procedure

NOTE: It can take approximately 20 seconds for this to happen after you close the circuit breaker. (c) Open this circuit breaker: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name B 3 C01046 AFCS SYS B FCC DC 1) Make sure that the "F/D" (in amber box) shows on the first officer's primary flight display. (d) Close this circuit breaker: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name B 3 C01046 AFCS SYS B FCC DC 1) Make sure that the "F/D" (in amber box) does not show on the first officer's primary flight display. (d) Do a check on these circuit breakers for the FCCA side: 1) Open this circuit breaker: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name C 5 C01041 AFCS SYS A SNSR EXC AC a) Make sure that the CDU display shows "SNSR EXC AC = 0 (±3)" on the FCCA side. 2) Close this circuit breaker: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name C 5 C01041 AFCS SYS A SNSR EXC AC a) Make sure that the CDU display shows "SNSR EXC AC = 26 (±3)" on the FCCA side. 22-11-00 3) Open this circuit breaker: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name D 1 C01049 AFCS SYS A WARN LIGHT (BAT) a) Make sure that the CDU display shows "WARN LIGHT (BAT) = 0 (±2)" on the FCCA side. 4) Close this circuit breaker: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name D 1 C01049 AFCS SYS A WARN LIGHT (BAT) a) Make sure that the CDU display shows "WARN LIGHT (BAT) = 28 (±2)" on the FCCA side. (e) Do a check on these circuit breakers for the FCCB side: 1) Open this circuit breaker: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name C 2 C01042 AFCS SYS B SNSR EXC AC a) Make sure that the CDU display shows "SNSR EXC AC = 0 (±3)" on the FCCB side. 2) Close this circuit breaker: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name C 2 C01042 AFCS SYS B SNSR EXC AC a) Make sure that the CDU display shows "SNSR EXC AC = 26 (±3)" on the FCCB side. 3) Open this circuit breaker: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name B 1 C00374 AFCS SYS B WARN LIGHT (BAT) a) Make sure that the CDU display shows "WARN LIGHT (BAT) = 0 (±2)" on the FCCB side. 4) Close this circuit breaker: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name B 1 C00374 AFCS SYS B WARN LIGHT (BAT) a) Make sure that the CDU display shows "WARN LIGHT (BAT) = 28 (±2)" on the FCCB side. 5) Push the LSK adjacent to EXIT until you get out of the BITE test. NOTE: If there are instructions on the CDU display, it is necessary to do the instructions that show on the CDU display. 22-11-00 F. Task Description

12. Sensor Excitation Test

A. General

(1) The Sensor Excitation Test does a check on the sensor excitation voltages for the A flight control computer (FCC-A) and the B flight control computer (FCC-B).

B. References

Reference Title 24-22-00-860-811 Supply Electrical Power (P/B 201) 24-22-00-860-812 Remove Electrical Power (P/B 201) 27-31-64-400-802 Elevator Feel and Centering Spring Installation (P/B 201) 29-11-00-860-801 Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization (P/B 201) 29-11-00-860-805 Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal (P/B 201)

SUBTASK 22-11-00-860-112 (4) Make sure that the VHF NAV and IRS switches, on the P5 forward overhead panel, are in the NORMAL positions. SUBTASK 22-11-00-860-113 (5) Set the left and right IRS select switches, on the P5 aft overhead panel, to the ALIGN or NAV position. SUBTASK 22-11-00-860-114 WARNING KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT AWAY FROM THE FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES. THE AILERONS, THE ELEVATORS, THE RUDDER, THE FLAPS, THE SLATS, THE SPOILERS, THE STABILIZER AND THE NOSE GEAR CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (6) Supply hydraulic power to hydraulic systems A and B. To supply hydraulic power, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801. NOTE: Hydraulic power is necessary for surface test.

A. General

(1) The Maintenance Monitor Test does a check on the maintenance monitor of the BITE. It makes sure that the monitor can record faults. This test also does a check on the DC power of the mode control panel.

(y) Set the first officer's flight director switch on the MCP to off. 22-11-00 (z) Remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name C 2 C01042 AFCS SYS B SNSR EXC AC F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3 Row Col Number Name D 1 C01399 PSEU PRI D 2 C01400 PSEU ALTN (aa) Stop for 20 seconds. A. General

(b) Push the left system annunciator lights on the P7 panel. (c) Make sure that these lights come on: 1) MACH TRIM FAIL light on the P5 forward overhead panel. 2) Master caution FLT CONT annunciator on the P7 panel. 3) Captain's master caution annunciator on the P7 panel. 4) First officer's master caution annunciator on the P7 panel. (d) Push the captain's master caution annunciator. (e) Make sure that these lights go off: 1) MACH TRIM FAIL light on the P5 forward overhead panel. 2) Master caution FLT CONT annunciator on the P7 panel. 3) Captain's master caution annunciator on the P7 panel. 4) First officer's master caution annunciator on the P7 panel. 22-11-00 (f) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name D 2 C01045 AFCS SYS A FCC DC (g) Stop for 50 seconds. (h) Make sure FD is removed from the Captain's Primary Flight Display. SUBTASK 22-11-00-980-006 (3) Do this check on the first officer's master caution annunciator: (a) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name B 3 C01046 AFCS SYS B FCC DC 1) Stop for 7 seconds. 2) Make sure that the MACH TRIM FAIL light, on the P5 forward overhead panel, stays off. (b) Push the right system annunciator lights on the P7 panel. (c) Make sure that these lights come on: 1) MACH TRIM FAIL light on the P5 forward overhead panel. 2) Master caution FLT CONT annunciator on the P7 panel. 3) Captain's master caution annunciator on the P7 panel. 4) First officer's master caution annunciator on the P7 panel. (d) Push the first officer's master caution annunciator. (e) Make sure that these lights go off: 1) MACH TRIM FAIL light on the P5 forward overhead panel. 2) Master caution FLT CONT annunciator on the P7 panel. 3) Captain's master caution annunciator on the P7 panel. 4) First officer's master caution annunciator on the P7 panel. (f) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name D 2 C01045 AFCS SYS A FCC DC (g) Stop for 7 seconds. (h) Make sure that these lights come on: 1) MACH TRIM FAIL light on the P5 forward overhead panel. 2) Master caution FLT CONT annunciator on the P7 panel. 3) Captain's master caution annunciator on the P7 panel. 4) First officer's master caution annunciator on the P7 panel. (i) Push the first officer's master caution annunciator. 1) Make sure that the MACH TRIM FAIL light, on the P5 forward overhead panel, stays on. 22-11-00 (j) Make sure that these lights go off. 1) Master caution FLT CONT annunciator on the P7 panel. 2) Captain's master caution annunciator on the P7 panel. 3) First officer's master caution annunciator on the P7 panel. (k) Remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name D 2 C01045 AFCS SYS A FCC DC F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name B 3 C01046 AFCS SYS B FCC DC (l) Stop for 50 seconds. 1) Make sure that the MACH TRIM FAIL light, on the P5 forward overhead panel, goes off. D. Location Zones

E. Access Panels

Number Name/Location 311BL Stabilizer Trim Access Door F. Prepare for the Test SUBTASK 22-11-00-860-366 (1) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3 Row Col Number Name D 18 C00451 LANDING GEAR AURAL WARN SUBTASK 22-11-00-860-367 (2) Set the autopilot stab trim cutout switch, on the control stand, to the CUTOUT positions. SUBTASK 22-11-00-860-368 (3) Make sure the VHF NAV and IRS switches, on the P5 forward overhead panel, are in the NORMAL positions. SUBTASK 22-11-00-860-369 (4) Set the left and right IRS select switches on the P5 aft overhead panel, to the ALIGN or NAV position. 22-11-00 SUBTASK 22-11-00-390-002 WARNING WHEN THE PITOT PROBES HAVE COVERS ON THEM, MAKE SURE THAT A PERSON ON THE GROUND CAN SEE THE COVERS. ALSO MAKE SURE YOU ATTACH A TAG TO THE LEFT CONTROL WHEEL IN THE FLIGHT COMPARTMENT AS A REMINDER THAT THE PITOT PROBES HAVE COVERS ON THEM. IF THE COVERS ARE NOT REMOVED FROM THE PITOT PROBES, INCORRECT AIRSPEED-SENSING AND ALTITUDE-SENSING SIGNALS CAN OCCUR. THIS CAN CAUSE DANGEROUS FLIGHT CONDITIONS. (5) At the two pitot probes on the vertical fin, do the following: (a) Seal the drain hole on each pitot probe. CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE PITOT PROBE HAS NO ADDED WEIGHT ON IT FROM THE TEST HOSE. THE WEIGHT OF THE TEST HOSE CAN BEND OR TWIST THE PITOT PROBE OUT OF TOLERANCE. (b) Connect the regulator, SPL-1742, or equivalent air data model test set, COM-1914, to the pitot probes. 1) Do this step for the regulator, SPL-1742: a) Connect the pressure lines from the regulator, SPL-1742, with the pitot test adapter, COM-1916, to the pitot probes. 2) Do this step for the air data model test set, COM-1914: a) Use the air data accessory kit, COM-25177, to connect the air data model test set, COM-1914, to the pitot test adapter, COM-1916. NOTE: The air data accessory kit, COM-25177, contains the hoses to connect the air data model test set, COM-1914, and the pitot test adapter, COM-1916. SUBTASK 22-11-00-010-008 (6) Open this access panel: Number Name/Location 311BL Stabilizer Trim Access Door SUBTASK 22-11-00-860-370 (7) Inside the aft unpressurized compartment, below the elevator feel computer, do the following: (a) Remove the restrictor valves from the bottom of the pitot lines. (b) If you are using the regulator, SPL-1742, or equivalent, do the following: 1) Connect the pressure gage lines from the regulator, SPL-1742, or equivalent, to the drain holes of the pitot lines. (c) If you are using the air data model test set, COM-1914, then do the following: 1) Install plugs over the ends of the pitot lines. 2) Install a highly visible streamer on the opening of the aft unpressurized compartment. NOTE: Make sure that you can easily see the streamer from the ground. This is to remind you to remove the plugs and install the restrictor valves again when the test is completed. 22-11-00 SUBTASK 22-11-00-860-371 WARNING KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT AWAY FROM THE FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES. THE AILERONS, ELEVATORS, RUDDER, FLAPS, SLATS, SPOILERS, STABILIZER, AND NOSE GEAR CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (8) Supply hydraulic power to hydraulic systems A and B. To supply hydraulic power, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801. SUBTASK 22-11-00-930-001 (9) Do these steps to set the B dimension (Figure 503): NOTE: The B dimension is measured between the center of the upper and lower Gimbal pins on the stabilizer trim jackscrew. To do this, one person must be in the tail of the airplane with a headset and the other person in the flight compartment. (a) Turn the stab trim wheel handle on the control stand to set the B dimension. (b) Use the trammel trammel bar, SPL-1677, to measure the B dimension. (c) Make sure that the B dimension is 39.89 ±0.01 in. (101.32 ±0.03 cm).

G. Elevator Single Authority Test

SUBTASK 22-11-00-740-051 (1) Push the INIT REF key on the Control Display Unit (CDU) keyboard. (a) Push the Line Select Key (LSK) that is adjacent to each selection: 1) INDEX 2) MAINT 3) DFCS 4) EXTENDED MAINTENANCE 5) RIGGING 6) ELEVATOR 7) ELEV AUTH SINGLE NOTE: This selection contains the ELEV AUTH SINGLE test. 8) During this test, do the instructions that show on the CDU display. 9) After you do the instructions that show on the CDU display, push the LSK that is adjacent to CONTINUE. 10) Test 51.16, set up the Feel System Condition II as follows: CAUTION OBEY THE LIMITS THAT FOLLOW. IF YOU DO NOT , DAMAGE TO THE ELEVATOR FEEL COMPUTER CAN OCCUR. a) Make sure that the pressure is no more then 5 psig (34.47 kPa), 474 knots (878 km/h) during the test. b) Operate the air data model test set, COM-1914, or regulator, SPL-1742, or equivalent, to pressurize the pitot system to 0.80 ±0.05 psig (5.52 ±0.34 kPa) = 180.16 ±10.00 knots (333.66 ±18.52 km/h). 11) Use the CDU keyboard to put code 100 into the scratchpad. 22-11-00 12) Push the LSK 6R. 13) Push the LSK that is adjacent to CONTINUE. 14) Make sure that the values for the A side are between the limits that show on the CDU display or in this task. 15) Do these steps: a) Set the B dimension to 38.46 ±0.01 in. (97.69 ±0.03 cm). b) Use the trammel trammel bar, SPL-1677, to measure the B dimension. c) Make sure that the B dimension is 38.46 ±0.01 in. (97.69 ±0.03 cm). 22-11-00-820-811Remote Light Sensor Input Test ATA 22 · Task 820-811

Task Description

25. Remote Light Sensor Input Test

A. General

(1) The Remote Light Sensor Input Test checks the input to the MCP that will change the LCD intensity. (2) The remote light sensors are on the forward part of the glareshield. The sensors face forward.

B. Location Zones

Zone Area 211 Flight Compartment - Left 212 Flight Compartment - Right

C. Procedure

SUBTASK 22-11-00-740-048 (1) Push the INIT REF key on the CDU keyboard. (2) Push the Line Select Key (LSK) that is adjacent to each selection: (a) INDEX (b) MAINT (c) DFCS (d) EXTENDED MAINTENANCE (e) SENSOR VALUES (f) DIGITAL SIGNALS (g) MCP (h) RLS-L. 22-11-00 (3) Point a flashlight at the notch on the front of the left remote light sensor (T507). (4) Verify that the value of the B channel is greater than 5.00. (5) Put an opaque lint-free fabric to the left remote light sensor (T507) so the sensor housing is completely covered. (6) Verify that the value of the B channel is less than 3.00. (7) Push the Line Select Key (LSK) that is adjacent to each selection: (a) PREV MENU (b) RLS-R. (8) Point a flashlight at the notch on the front of the right remote light sensor (T508). (9) Verify that the value of the B channel is greater than 5.00. (10) Put an opaque lint-free fabric to the right remote light sensor (T508) so the sensor housing is completely covered. (11) Verify that the value of the B channel is less than 3.00. (12) Push the Line Select Key (LSK) that is adjacent to each selection: (a) EXIT (b) EXITon TEST COMPLETE screen. (c) EXIT after having complied with the instructions on END OF DFCS BITE screen.

C. Procedure

SUBTASK 22-11-00-740-050 (1) Push the INIT REF key on the Control Display Unit (CDU) keyboard. NOTE: Use “NEXT PAGE” or “PREVIOUS PAGE” key to change pages. (c) Push “CONTINUE on “AUTOTEST INITIALIZATION” screen and run the test by following the instructions on the CDU. (d) VERIFY , “ALL TEST PASSED” message displays on the CDU. NOTE: Some test may be completed so fast that they may not be visible on the CDU. NOTE: Test can be considered as having passed unless a “TEST FAILED” message appeared. (e) Push “CONTINUE” on test “SUMMARY” screen. (f) Push “CONTINUE” after having complied with the instructions “TURN OFF HYD A-B”. (g) Push “EXIT” on “TEST COMPLETE” screen. (h) Push “EXIT” after having complied with the instructions on “END OF DFCS BITE” screen. Task Description

2. Roll Control Wheel Steering Force Transducer - Deactivation (Figure 202)

A. General

(1) This procedure removes electrical power and hydraulic pressure to the Roll Control Wheel Steering Force Transducer.

B. References

C. Tools/Equipment

Reference Description STD-858 Tag - DO NOT OPERATE

E. Roll Control Wheel Steering Force Transducer Deactivation

SUBTASK 22-11-11-020-005 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT CONTROLS SURFACES. MAKE SURE THAT THE INBOARD FAN DUCT COWL AND THE INBOARD AND OUTBOARD THRUST REVERSERS ARE CLOSED. THE FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (1) Remove hydraulic power from systems A and B. (a) Do this task:Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805. 22-11-11-000-801Roll Force Transducer Removal ATA 22 · Task 000-801

Task Description

2. Roll Force Transducer Removal (Figure 401)

A. Location Zones

Zone Area 112 Area Forward of Nose Landing Gear Wheel Well

B. Access Panels

Number Name/Location 112A Forward Access Door

C. Prepare for the Removal

SUBTASK 22-11-11-860-024 (1) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name C 5 C01041 AFCS SYS A SNSR EXC AC D 1 C01049 AFCS SYS A WARN LIGHT (BAT) D 2 C01045 AFCS SYS A FCC DC F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name B 1 C00374 AFCS SYS B WARN LIGHT (BAT) B 3 C01046 AFCS SYS B FCC DC C 2 C01042 AFCS SYS B SNSR EXC AC SUBTASK 22-11-11-860-025 (2) Install the DO-NOT OPERATE tags to the control columns. SUBTASK 22-11-11-010-002 (3) To get access to the roll force transducer, open this access door: Number Name/Location 112A Forward Access Door

D. Procedure

SUBTASK 22-11-11-020-001 (1) Disconnect the connectors of the roll force transducer [1]. SUBTASK 22-11-11-020-002 (2) For the upper spool, do these steps to remove the cable [5] of the roll force transducer [1]: 22-11-11 (a) Remove the screws [9], screw [15], bolt [14], washers [7], washers [10], nut [6], spacer [13], cable clamps [11] and plugs [12]. (b) Wind the cable [5] of the roll force transducer [1] off the shaft assembly of the upper spool. NOTE: Write down the direction of the cable. SUBTASK 22-11-11-020-003 (3) For the lower spool, do these steps to remove the cable [5] of the roll force transducer [1]: (a) Remove the nuts [6], bolt [17], screws [9], washers [10], cable clamps [11], cable clamp [16] and plugs [12]. (b) Wind the cable [5] of the roll force transducer [1] off the shaft assembly of the lower spool. NOTE: Write down the direction of the cable. SUBTASK 22-11-11-020-004 (4) Do these steps to remove the roll force transducer [1]: (a) Remove the mounting bolts [8], washers [7] and nuts [6] that attach the roll force transducer [1] to the aileron drum assembly. (b) Remove the roll force transducer [1].

E. Prepare for the Installation

SUBTASK 22-11-11-860-028 (1) Make sure that these circuit breakers are open and have safety tags: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name C 5 C01041 AFCS SYS A SNSR EXC AC D 1 C01049 AFCS SYS A WARN LIGHT (BAT) D 2 C01045 AFCS SYS A FCC DC F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name B 1 C00374 AFCS SYS B WARN LIGHT (BAT) B 3 C01046 AFCS SYS B FCC DC C 2 C01042 AFCS SYS B SNSR EXC AC F. Roll Force Transducer Installation SUBTASK 22-11-11-800-001 (1) Use the 0.0 - 0.5 Inch feeler gauge, STD-1107, to make a clearance (two locations) between the sensor shaft and the aileron drum shaft. RYR 006, 007; AIRPLANES WITH 251A1814-3, -4, -5 AILERON DRUM SHAFT ASSEMBLY . (a) Make sure that each clearance is between 0.021 in. (0.533 mm) and 0.024 in. (0.610 mm). 22-11-11 RYR 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999; AIRPLANES WITH 251A1814-9, -10, -12 AILERON DRUM SHAFT ASSEMBLY . (b) Make sure that each clearance is between 0.057 in. (1.448 mm) and 0.060 in. (1.524 mm). RYR ALL SUBTASK 22-11-11-820-001 (2) For the non-adjustable end of the roll force transducer [1], do these steps: (a) Hold the roll force transducer [1] in its position for installation. (b) Install the mounting bolt [8], washer [7], and nut [6]. SUBTASK 22-11-11-420-001 (3) For the adjustable end of the roll force transducer [1], do these steps: (a) Hold the roll force transducer [1] in its position for installation. (b) Install the mounting bolt [8], washer [7], and nut [6]. SUBTASK 22-11-11-420-002 (4) Do these steps to install the lower cable [5] of the roll force transducer [1] in the upper spool: (a) Attach the cable [5] with the cable clamp [11] below the roll force transducer [1]. 1) Install the bolt [14], washers [7], spacer [13], nut [6], and plug [12]. 2) Make sure that you do not pull the cable [5] tightly. (b) Wind the cable [5] around the upper spool, approximately 4 turns, in the CCW direction (as seen from the bottom) from the top to the bottom of the spool. (c) Turn the control wheel, to the limit, in the direction to tighten the cable [5] around the spool. (d) Attach the cable [5] with the cable clamps [11] on the bracket. 1) Install the screw [9], screw [15], washers [10], and plugs [12]. (e) Turn the control wheel clockwise and then counter-clockwise, to the limit, for two or three times. 1) Make sure that the cable [5] does not prevent the movement. 2) If it is necessary, adjust the cable [5] in the bracket. SUBTASK 22-11-11-420-003 (5) Do these steps to install the top cable [5] of the roll force transducer [1] in the lower spool: (a) Attach the cable [5] with the cable clamp [11] adjacent to the roll force transducer [1]. 1) Install the washer [10], nut [6], and plug [12]. (b) Attach the cable [5] with the cable clamp [11] on the spool bracket of the lower flange. 1) Install the bolt [17], washer [10], nut [6], and plug [12]. 2) Make sure that you do not pull the cable [5] tightly. (c) Wind the cable [5] around the lower spool, approximately 4.5 turns, in the CW direction (as seen from the bottom) from the top to the bottom of the spool. (d) Turn the control wheel, to the limit, in the direction to tighten the cable [5] around the spool. (e) Attach the cable [5] with the cable clamp [11], cable clamp [16] on the bracket. 22-11-11 1) Install the screws [9], washers [10], and plugs [12]. (f) Turn the control wheel clockwise and then counter-clockwise, to the limit, for two or three times. 1) Make sure that the cable [5] does not prevent the movement. 2) Make sure that the cable [5] is not too loose to contact bolt [17]. 3) If it is necessary, adjust the cable [5] in the bracket. SUBTASK 22-11-11-420-004 (6) Connect the roll force transducer connectors. SUBTASK 22-11-11-800-002 (7) Remove the 0.0 - 0.5 Inch feeler gauge, STD-1107, (two locations) between the sensor shaft and the aileron drum shaft. RYR 006, 007; AIRPLANES WITH 251A1814-3, -4, -5 AILERON DRUM SHAFT ASSEMBLY . (a) Make sure that each clearance is between 0.021 in. (0.533 mm) and 0.024 in. (0.610 mm). RYR 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999; AIRPLANES WITH 251A1814-9, -10, -12 AILERON DRUM SHAFT ASSEMBLY . (b) Make sure that each clearance is between 0.057 in. (1.448 mm) and 0.060 in. (1.524 mm). RYR ALL SUBTASK 22-11-11-860-029 (8) Remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name C 5 C01041 AFCS SYS A SNSR EXC AC D 1 C01049 AFCS SYS A WARN LIGHT (BAT) F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name B 1 C00374 AFCS SYS B WARN LIGHT (BAT) C 2 C01042 AFCS SYS B SNSR EXC AC SUBTASK 22-11-11-860-041 (9) Remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name D 2 C01045 AFCS SYS A FCC DC F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name B 3 C01046 AFCS SYS B FCC DC SUBTASK 22-11-11-820-002 (10) Do this task: Roll Force Transducer Adjustment and Test, TASK 22-11-11-820-801. 22-11-11 SUBTASK 22-11-11-740-003 (11) Do this task: Roll Force Transducer Test, TASK 22-11-11-740-801. SUBTASK 22-11-11-800-003 (12) Remove the DO NOT OPERATE tags, STD-858, from the control columns. SUBTASK 22-11-11-410-002 (13) Close this access door: Number Name/Location 112A Forward Access Door

A. References

Reference Title 20-10-44-000-801 Lockwire, Cotter Pins, and Lockrings - Removal (P/B 401) 20-10-44-400-801 Lockwire, Cotter Pins, and Lockrings - Installation (P/B 401) 22-11-00-820-807 Roll Control Wheel Steering Rigging Test (P/B 501) 29-11-00-860-801 Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization (P/B 201) 29-11-00-860-805 Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal (P/B 201)

B. Tools/Equipment

NOTE: When more than one tool part number is listed under the same "Reference" number, the tools shown are alternates to each other within the same airplane series. Tool part numbers that are replaced or non-procurable are preceded by "Opt:", which stands for Optional. Reference Description SPL-1674 Assembly - Adapter, Control Wheel, Torque and Force Test Part #: C27060-22 Supplier: 81205 Opt Part #: C27060-1 Supplier: 81205 Opt Part #: F72867-1 Supplier: 81205 STD-858 Tag - DO NOT OPERATE STD-1107 Gauge - Feeler, 0.0 - 0.5 Inch, Readable to 1/1000th STD-1293 Wrench - Torque, 100 in-lbs, +/-5% accuracy

C. Location Zones

Zone Area 112 Area Forward of Nose Landing Gear Wheel Well 211 Flight Compartment - Left 212 Flight Compartment - Right

D. Access Panels

Number Name/Location 112A Forward Access Door

E. Prepare for the Adjustment

SUBTASK 22-11-11-010-001 (1) To get access to the roll force transducer, open this access door: Number Name/Location 112A Forward Access Door 22-11-11 SUBTASK 22-11-11-860-032 (2) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3 Row Col Number Name D 18 C00451 LANDING GEAR AURAL WARN SUBTASK 22-11-11-860-002 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT ALL PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF ALL THE HYDRAULIC COMPONENTS WHEN POWER IS ON. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY DURING THE PRESSURIZATION OF A HYDRAULIC SYSTEM. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONNEL OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (3) Supply hydraulic power to hydraulic systems A and B (TASK 29-11-00-860-801). SUBTASK 22-11-11-980-001 (4) Do these steps to put the control wheel to the center: NOTE: The power control units must be serviceable for the correct adjustment of the cables in relation to the roll force transducer. (a) Turn the control wheel clockwise 30 degrees. (b) Turn the control wheel counter-clockwise 30 degrees. (c) Slowly turn the control wheel to the center. SUBTASK 22-11-11-860-003 (5) Attach the DO NOT OPERATE tags, STD-858, to the control columns. SUBTASK 22-11-11-860-004 (6) Set the aileron trim to 0.0 unit. SUBTASK 22-11-11-860-005 (7) Set the autopilot stab trim cutout switch, on the control stand, to the CUTOUT position. SUBTASK 22-11-11-860-006 (8) Make sure that the VHF NAV and IRS switches, on the P5 forward overhead panel, are in the NORMAL positions. SUBTASK 22-11-11-860-007 (9) Set the left and right IRS select switches, on the P5 aft overhead panel, to the ALIGN or NAV position. F. Roll Force Transducer Adjustment and Test NOTE: Two persons are necessary for this task. SUBTASK 22-11-11-740-001 (1) Do these steps to get access to DFCS BITE: (a) Push the INIT REF key on the CDU keyboard. (b) Push the Line Select Key (LSK) that is adjacent to each selection: NOTE: If the CONTINUE shows during the BITE test, then do the instructions that show on the CDU display before you push the LSK that is adjacent to CONTINUE. Use the NEXT PAGE or PREV PAGE key to change page if it is necessary. 1) INDEX 2) MAINT 22-11-11 3) DFCS 4) EXTENDED MAINTENANCE 5) RIGGING 6) CWS 7) ROLL CWS 8) Do the instructions that show on the CDU display until test 55.18. a) Test 55.18, RCWS SENSOR (VAC), Limits: -0.15 to +0.15. NOTE: Use this CDU display to do the adjustment for the roll force transducer. SUBTASK 22-11-11-820-003 WARNING DO NOT PUSH THE LSK THAT IS ADJACENT TO (CONTINUE) ON TEST 55.18 WHEN YOU ADJUST THE ROLL FORCE TRANSDUCER. THE CABLES, CONTROL WHEEL AND FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES CAN MOVE WHEN YOU PUSH THE LSK THAT IS ADJACENT TO (CONTINUE). THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (2) Do these steps to adjust the roll force transducer: (a) Use the 0.0 - 0.5 Inch feeler gauge, STD-1107, to make a clearance (two locations) between the sensor shaft and the aileron drum shaft. 1) If you cannot get access to this area, then remove the bolt [4], nut [1], washers [5], spacer [8], clamp [7] and plug [6]. RYR 006, 007 (b) Make sure that each clearance is between 0.021 in. (0.533 mm) and 0.024 in. (0.610 mm). RYR 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999 (c) Make sure that each clearance is between 0.057 in. (1.448 mm) and 0.060 in. (1.524 mm). RYR ALL (d) Remove the mounting bolt [3], washer [2] and nut [1]. (e) If the voltages on the CDU display (Test 55.18) for the A and B sides are not within ±0.08 VAC, do these steps: NOTE: For minimum error, you must hold the roll force transducer horizontally when you read the voltage. 1) Make sure that there is no external force applied to the roll force transducer (For example, if the cable is tightly pulled, then it can cause the voltage to increase). 2) Remove lockwires from the locknuts, fine adjustment nut and the tab washer. To remove it, do this task: Lockwire, Cotter Pins, and Lockrings - Removal, TASK 20-10-44-000-801. 3) Loosen the locknuts. 4) Turn the coarse adjustment (rod end) until the voltages on the CDU for the A and B sides are within ±0.08 VAC.. NOTE: The coarse adjustment is approximately 0.016 in. (0.406 mm) for each turn. 22-11-11 (f) Record the voltage. (g) Turn the coarse adjustment (rod end) until the mounting hole is parallel to the mounting hole. (h) Install the mounting bolt [3], washer [2] and nut [1]. (i) Make sure that the voltage is within ±0.01 VAC of the voltage you recorded earlier. NOTE: Use the fine adjustment nut if necessary. (j) Push the tab washer against the end of the roll force transducer. (k) Tighten the locknut on the adjustable sleeve. (l) Tighten the locknut on the rod end. (m) For the locknuts, fine adjustment nut and the tab washer, do this task: Lockwire, Cotter Pins, and Lockrings - Installation, TASK 20-10-44-400-801. (n) Remove the 0.0 - 0.5 Inch feeler gauge, STD-1107 (2 locations) between the sensor shaft and the aileron drum shaft. 1) Install the bolt [4], nut [1], washers [5], spacer [8], clamp [7] and plug [6] if you remove them earlier. RYR 006, 007 (o) Make sure that each clearance is between 0.021 in. (0.533 mm) and 0.024 in. (0.610 mm) RYR 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999 (p) Make sure that each clearance is between 0.057 in. (1.448 mm) and 0.060 in. (1.524 mm) RYR ALL (q) Do the following, to check the adjustments: WARNING KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT AWAY FROM THE ROLL CONTROL-WHEEL STEERING FORCE-TRANSDUCER. THE CABLES, CONTROL WHEEL AND FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES CAN MOVE WHEN YOU PUSH THE LSK THAT IS ADJACENT TO (CONTINUE). THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . 1) Push the LSK that is adjacent to <CONTINUE (on the CDU display - Test 55.18). a) Do the instructions that show on the CDU display to complete the ROLL CWS test. b) Make sure that the values for the A and B sides are between the limits that show on the CDU display. NOTE: For detailed data about the ROLL CWS rigging test, refer to "Roll Control Wheel Steering Rigging Test" in (TASK 22-11-00-820-807). c) To continue the test, you must install the control wheel torque wrench adapter, SPL-1674. 22-11-11 d) When the CDU display shows "Torque wheel clockwise (or counter-clockwise) to x LBS on scale", use the control wheel torque wrench , STD-1293, to measure the force that you put on the control wheel. NOTE: Where x is a number. 2) Remove the control wheel torque wrench adapter, SPL-1674, when you complete the ROLL CWS test.

G. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 22-11-11-860-030 (2) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3 Row Col Number Name D 18 C00451 LANDING GEAR AURAL WARN SUBTASK 22-11-11-860-010 (3) Set the autopilot stab trim cutout switch, on the control stand, to the NORMAL position. SUBTASK 22-11-11-860-011 (4) Remove hydraulic power from hydraulic systems A and B (TASK 29-11-00-860-805). SUBTASK 22-11-11-860-013 (5) Remove the DO NOT OPERATE tags, STD-858, on the control columns. SUBTASK 22-11-11-410-001 (6) Close this access panel: Number Name/Location 112A Forward Access Door

A. References

Reference Title 24-22-00-860-811 Supply Electrical Power (P/B 201) 24-22-00-860-812 Remove Electrical Power (P/B 201) 29-11-00-860-801 Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization (P/B 201) 29-11-00-860-805 Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal (P/B 201)

SUBTASK 22-11-11-860-014 (1) Do this task: Supply Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-811. SUBTASK 22-11-11-860-033 (2) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3 Row Col Number Name D 18 C00451 LANDING GEAR AURAL WARN SUBTASK 22-11-11-860-015 (3) Set the autopilot stab trim cutout switch, on the control stand, to the CUTOUT position. SUBTASK 22-11-11-860-018 WARNING KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT AWAY FROM THE FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES. THE AILERONS, ELEVATORS, RUDDER, FLAPS, SLATS, SPOILERS, STABILIZER AND NOSE GEAR CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . D. Procedure

SUBTASK 22-11-11-740-002 (1) Do this BITE test: (a) Push the INIT REF key on the CDU keyboard. 22-11-11 (b) Push the Line Select Key (LSK) that is adjacent to each selection: NOTE: If the CONTINUE shows during the BITE test, then do the instructions that show on the CDU display before you push the LSK that is adjacent to CONTINUE. Use the NEXT PAGE or PREV PAGE key to change page if it is necessary. 1) INDEX 2) MAINT 3) DFCS 4) LRU REPLACEMENT TESTS 5) CHANNEL A AND B 6) ROLL SENS 7) Do the instructions that show on the CDU display to complete the test. 8) Make sure that the test is completed with no failure or the "TEST FAILED" message does not show.

G. A/P Solenoid and Electrohydraulic Servo Valves Installation

SUBTASK 22-11-12-420-001 (1) Do these steps to install the solenoid valve [1]: (a) Install the new seal-u-cup [5] on the solenoid valve [1]. 22-11-12 1) Make sure that you install the larger diameter of the seal-u-cup [5] against the solenoid valve [1]. (b) Apply a layer of the hydraulic fluid, D00153, or MCS 352B fluid, D00054, to the two sides of the gasket plate [4]. (c) Put the new gasket plate [4] in the correct position. (d) Put the solenoid valve [1] in its position for installation. (e) Install the screws [2] and washers [3] that attach the solenoid valve [1]. (f) Tighten the screws [2] to 50 in-lb (5.6 N·m) to 70 in-lb (7.9 N·m). 1) Install MS20995C20 lockwire, G50225, on the screws [2] with double twist method. 2) Apply compound, A00226, to the end of the MS20995C20 lockwire, G50225. SUBTASK 22-11-12-420-002 (2) Do these steps to install the electrohydraulic servo valve [7]: (a) Install the new seal-u-cup [5] on the electrohydraulic servo valve [7]. 1) Make sure that you install the larger diameter of the seal-u-cup [5] against the electrohydraulic servo valve [7]. (b) Apply a layer of the hydraulic fluid, D00153, or MCS 352B fluid, D00054, to the two sides of the gasket plate [6]. (c) Put the new gasket plate [6] in the correct position. (d) Put the electrohydraulic servo valve [7] in its position for installation. (e) Install the screws [8] and washers [9] that attach the electrohydraulic servo valve [7]. (f) Tighten the screws [8] to 50 in-lb (5.6 N·m) to 70 in-lb (7.9 N·m). 1) Install MS20995C20 lockwire, G50225, on the screws [8] with double twist method. 2) Apply compound, A00226, to the end of the MS20995C20 lockwire, G50225. THE AILERONS, THE ELEVATORS, THE RUDDER, THE FLAPS, THE SLATS, THE SPOILERS, THE STABILIZER AND THE NOSE GEAR CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. I. Post Installation Test

SUBTASK 22-11-12-740-001 (1) Do this Built-In-Test Equipment (BITE) test: (a) Push the INIT REF key on the Control Display Unit (CDU) keyboard. (b) Push the Line Select Key (LSK) that is adjacent to each selection: NOTE: If the CONTINUE shows during the BITE test, do the instructions that show on the CDU display before the LSK is pushed that is adjacent to CONTINUE. Use the NEXT PAGE or PREV PAGE key to change page if it is necessary. 1) INDEX 2) MAINT 3) DFCS 4) EXTENDED MAINTENANCE 5) BITE LIBRARY TEST 6) Make a selection for the applicable channel: NOTE: A/P aileron actuator A and A/P elevator actuator A have interfaces with the Flight Control Computer (FCC) A (Channel A). A/P aileron actuator B and A/P elevator actuator B have interfaces with the FCC B (Channel B). a) CHANNEL A b) CHANNEL B c) CHANNEL A AND B. 7) RUN SELECT LIBRARY TESTS 8) 30 ELEV CONTROL or 31 AIL CONTROL NOTE: 30 ELEV CONTROL is for the A/P elevator actuators and 31 AIL CONTROL is for the A/P aileron actuators. 9) EXECUTE. (c) Do the instructions that show on the CDU to complete the test. (d) Make sure that the test is completed with no failure or the "TEST FAILED" message does not show. SUBTASK 22-11-12-210-001 (2) Visually examine the solenoid valve [1] and electrohydraulic servo valve [7]. (a) Make sure that there is no hydraulic leak.

SUBTASK 22-11-24-860-002 (2) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name C 4 C00456 AFCS SYS A MACH TRIM AC D 4 C00457 AFCS SYS A MACH TRIM DC 22-11-24 F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name B 2 C01064 AFCS SYS B MACH TRIM DC C 1 C01037 AFCS SYS B MACH TRIM AC SUBTASK 22-11-24-010-001 (3) To get access to the mach trim actuator [1], open this access panel: Number Name/Location 318BR T ailcone Access Door F. Mach Trim Actuator Removal SUBTASK 22-11-24-820-001 (1) Put rigging pin E-5 from the kit of rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, into its hole in the aft control quadrant. SUBTASK 22-11-24-020-001 (2) Disconnect the electrical connector [4] from the mach trim actuator [1]. SUBTASK 22-11-24-020-003 (5) Remove the bolts [2] that attach the mach trim actuator [1] to the elevator feel and centering unit. SUBTASK 22-11-24-020-004 (6) Remove the mach trim actuator [1], washers [9], and bearings [10].

22-11-24-400-801Mach Trim Actuator Installation ATA 22 · Task 400-801

Task Description

3. Mach Trim Actuator Installation (Figure 401)

A. References

Reference Title 22-11-24-740-801 Mach Trim Actuator Installation Test (P/B 501) SOPM 20-50-03 Bearing and Bushing Replacement

B. Tools/Equipment

NOTE: When more than one tool part number is listed under the same "Reference" number, the tools shown are alternates to each other within the same airplane series. Tool part numbers that are replaced or non-procurable are preceded by "Opt:", which stands for Optional. Reference Description SPL-1585 Kit - Rigging Pin Part #: F70207-109 Supplier: 81205

C. Consumable Materials

D. Expendables/Parts

E. Location Zones

Zone Area 315 APU Compartment - Left 316 APU Compartment - Right F. Access Panels Number Name/Location 318BR T ailcone Access Door

G. Mach Trim Actuator Installation

SUBTASK 22-11-24-820-002 (1) Put rigging pin E-5 from the kit of rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, into its hole in the aft control quadrant. 22-11-24 SUBTASK 22-11-24-420-001 (2) Make sure that the bearings and washer are in the correct position at the mounting points on the feel and centering unit. NOTE: Move the feel and centering unit up or down to put the actuator arm in position. If it is necessary, remove the rigging pin and push the elevator control surface up, or pull aft on the control column. SUBTASK 22-11-24-420-002 (3) Do these steps to install the mach trim actuator [1]: (a) Install the bearings [10] into the bearing lugs. (b) Apply sealant, A00247, to the bearings [10] (SOPM 20-50-03). (c) Put the mach trim actuator [1] with the washers [9] in their positions. (d) Install the bolts [2] on the sides. SUBTASK 22-11-24-420-003 (4) Make sure that the crank arm of the neutral shift mechanism can move freely in the clevis of the mach trim actuator [1] arm. SUBTASK 22-11-24-420-004 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT YOU TURN THE NEUTRAL SHIFT CRANK IN THE UP DIRECTION. IF YOU INSTALL THE NEUTRAL SHIFT CRANK INCORRECTLY , THE STABILIZER CAN MOVE QUICKLY WHEN YOU ENGAGE THE AUTOPILOT . THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (5) Install the bolt assembly [3]. (a) Install the bolt assembly [3] and washer [11] from the left to the right side. (b) Install the washer [5] and nut [6]. NOTE: This is the larger nut. (c) Tighten the nut [6] to 85 in-lb (9.6 N·m) - 100 in-lb (11.3 N·m). CAUTION DO NOT CHANGE THE TORQUE ON THE LARGE NUT [6] AFTER YOU TIGHTEN THE SMALL NUT [8]. IF CHANGED, THE TORQUE VALUE WILL BE INCORRECT . (d) Install the washer [7] and nut [8]. (e) Tighten the nut [8] to 30 in-lb (3.4 N·m) - 35 in-lb (4.0 N·m). SUBTASK 22-11-24-420-005 (6) Tighten the bolts [2] on the sides of the mach trim actuator [1] to 20 in-lb (2.3 N·m) - 25 in-lb (2.8 N·m). SUBTASK 22-11-24-420-007 (7) Install MS20995NC32 lockwire, G01912, on the bolts [2] with double twist method. SUBTASK 22-11-24-420-006 (8) Connect the electrical connector [4] to the mach trim actuator [1]. SUBTASK 22-11-24-940-001 (9) Remove the rigging pin E-5 from the aft control quadrant. 22-11-24

H. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

(b) Install the reducer [10] and O-ring [11] in the pressure port on the autopilot aileron actuator A [1] or autopilot aileron actuator B [1]. 1) Tighten the reducer [10] to 165 in-lb (18.6 N·m) - 175 in-lb (19.8 N·m). (c) Install the union [9] and O-ring [11] in the port on the autopilot aileron actuator A [1] or autopilot aileron actuator B [1]. 1) Tighten the union [9] to 165 in-lb (18.6 N·m) - 175 in-lb (19.8 N·m). (b) Install the union [8] and O-ring [3] in the pressure port on the autopilot aileron actuator B [1]. 22-11-25 1) Tighten the union [8] to 105 in-lb (11.9 N·m) - 115 in-lb (13 N·m). (c) Install the fitting [2], retainer [6], and swivel nut [7]. 1) Tighten the swivel nut [7] to 105 in-lb (11.9 N·m) - 115 in-lb (13 N·m). (b) Adjust the length of the rod assembly [7] until the bolt [1] can go smoothly through the rod and the autopilot aileron actuator A lever assembly [6]. (c) Make sure that you can see the bearing threads of the rod end through the inspection hole at the end of the rod assembly [7]. 1) Adjust the rod assembly if it is necessary. NOTE: You can see the movement at the inboard end of the right aileron. (f) Make sure that the values for the A side and B side are at 0 ±0.08 VAC that show on the CDU display (Test 52.04). Use the NEXT PAGE or PREV PAGE key to change page if it is necessary. 1) INDEX 2) MAINT 22-11-25 3) DFCS 4) EXTENDED MAINTENANCE 5) BITE LIBRARY TEST 6) Make a selection for the applicable channel: NOTE: A/P (Autopilot) aileron actuator A has interface with the Flight Control Computer (FCC) A (Channel A). A/P aileron actuator B has interface with the FCC B (Channel B). a) CHANNEL A b) CHANNEL B c) CHANNEL A AND B. 7) RUN SELECT LIBRARY TESTS 8) 31 AIL CONTROL 9) EXECUTE 10) Do the instructions that show on the CDU to complete the test. 11) Make sure that the test is completed with no failure or the "TEST FAILED" message does not show.

22-11-25-200-801Autopilot Aileron Actuator Linkage Inspection ATA 22 · Task 200-801

Task Description

1. Autopilot Aileron Actuator Linkage Inspection (Figure 601)

A. General

(1) This procedure is for an inspection of the worn areas of the autopilot aileron actuator linkage. To do this check, you must remove the autopilot aileron actuator linkage. Usually you use this procedure when you do the overhaul of the autopilot aileron actuator linkage. To get access to the components or to replace the components during the inspection, refer to (Autopilot Aileron Actuator Removal, TASK 22-11-25-000-801)

B. References

Reference Title 22-11-25-000-801 Autopilot Aileron Actuator Removal (P/B 401)

C. Tools/Equipment

Reference Description STD-1096 Micrometer - Depth, 0-1 inch, Readable to 1/1000 inch STD-1097 Caliper - Vernier, 0-6 inch, Readable to 1/1000 inch

D. Procedure

SUBTASK 22-11-25-020-003 (1) Remove the parts that are necessary for inspection. SUBTASK 22-11-25-200-003 (2) Examine the parts: (a) Use a micrometer (0-1 inch, readable to 1/1000 inch), STD-1096 or a vernier caliper (0 - 6 inch, readable to 1/1000 inch), STD-1097 to measure the parts. (b) Compare the dimensions you measured with the permitted dimensions shown in (Figure 601). (c) Repair or replace the parts that are out of the tolerance. SUBTASK 22-11-25-420-001 (3) Install the parts.

E. Autopilot Elevator Actuator Removal

SUBTASK 22-11-26-020-001 (1) Disconnect the hydraulic lines from the hydraulic ports on the autopilot elevator actuator [1]. SUBTASK 22-11-26-480-001 (2) Install protective covers and plugs on the hydraulic lines and the hydraulic ports. SUBTASK 22-11-26-020-002 (3) Remove the electrical connector from the autopilot elevator actuator [1]. SUBTASK 22-11-26-020-004 (4) Remove the hydraulic pressure switch [11] (TASK 22-11-40-000-801). SUBTASK 22-11-26-020-005 (5) Do these steps to remove the autopilot elevator actuator [1]: (a) Remove the clamp bolt [6], washer [7], and nut [8] that attach the lever assembly [13] or lever assembly [12] to the autopilot elevator actuator [1]. (b) Remove the nut [4] and washer [5] that attach the output shaft of the autopilot elevator actuator [1] to the lever assembly [13] or lever assembly [12]. (c) Move the lever assembly [13] or lever assembly [12] away from the autopilot elevator actuator [1]. (d) Remove the mounting bolts [2] and washer [3] that hold the autopilot elevator actuator [1]. (e) Remove the autopilot elevator actuator [1]. (f) Remove the reducer [9] and reducer [10] from the hydraulic ports on the autopilot elevator actuator [1]. 1) Remove and discard the packings [14]. SUBTASK 22-11-26-480-002 (6) Install protective plugs on the hydraulic ports.

G. Autopilot Elevator Actuator Installation

SUBTASK 22-11-26-420-001 (1) Lightly lubricate the new packings [14] with hydraulic fluid, D00153. SUBTASK 22-11-26-420-013 (2) Install the new packings [14] on the reducer [9] and reducer [10]. SUBTASK 22-11-26-080-001 (3) Remove the protective plugs from the hydraulic ports. SUBTASK 22-11-26-420-011 (4) Install the reducer [9] and reducer [10] in the hydraulic ports on the autopilot elevator actuator [1]. 22-11-26 (a) Tighten the reducer [9] and reducer [10] to 161.5 in-lb (18.2 N·m) - 178.5 in-lb (20.2 N·m). SUBTASK 22-11-26-800-001 (5) Fill the autopilot elevator actuator [1] with hydraulic fluid, D00153. SUBTASK 22-11-26-480-003 (6) Install protective plugs on the reducer [9] and reducer [10]. SUBTASK 22-11-26-420-002 (7) Hold the autopilot elevator actuator [1] in its position for installation. SUBTASK 22-11-26-420-012 (8) Install the mounting bolts [2] and washers [3]. (a) Make sure that the countersunk side of the washer [3] is against the head of the mounting bolt [2]. SUBTASK 22-11-26-200-007 (9) Do these steps to examine the shear rivets on the lever assembly [12] or lever assembly [13]: (a) Make sure that there is no unwanted materials in the shear rivet holes. (b) Do this step to check for deformation of the rivet: 1) Insert a 0.0375 in. (0.95 mm) – 0.0395 in. (1.0 mm) diameter pin in the inspection hole in each rivet. 2) Make sure that the pin moves freely while applying force in both directions to the lever assembly. 3) If the pin does not move freely, replace the shear rivets. SUBTASK 22-11-26-420-003 (10) Install the lever assembly [13] or lever assembly [12]: (a) Place the lever assembly [13] or lever assembly [12] on the autopilot elevator actuator [1]. (b) Carefully align the splines. NOTE: The position of a tooth not on the spline provides the access. (c) Install the clamp bolt [6], washer [7], and nut [8] to attach the lever assembly [13] or lever assembly [12] to the autopilot elevator actuator [1]. 1) Tighten the nut [8] to 33 in-lb (3.7 N·m) - 35 in-lb (4.0 N·m). (d) Install the washer [5] and nut [4] on the output shaft of the autopilot elevator actuator [1]. (e) Tighten the nut [4] on the output shaft. (f) Tighten the clamp bolt [6]. SUBTASK 22-11-26-420-004 (11) Connect the hydraulic lines: (a) Remove the plugs from the hydraulic lines and the plugs on the reducer [9] and reducer [10]. (b) Connect the hydraulic lines to the hydraulic ports on the autopilot elevator actuator [1]. SUBTASK 22-11-26-420-005 (12) Install the hydraulic pressure switch [11] (TASK 22-11-40-400-801). SUBTASK 22-11-26-420-006 (13) Connect the electrical connector for the autopilot elevator actuator [1]. 22-11-26 SUBTASK 22-11-26-860-005 (14) Remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name C 4 C00456 AFCS SYS A MACH TRIM AC C 5 C01041 AFCS SYS A SNSR EXC AC D 1 C01049 AFCS SYS A WARN LIGHT (BAT) D 3 C01048 AFCS SYS A ENGAGE INTLK D 4 C00457 AFCS SYS A MACH TRIM DC D 5 C01044 AFCS MCP DC 1 F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name B 1 C00374 AFCS SYS B WARN LIGHT (BAT) B 2 C01064 AFCS SYS B MACH TRIM DC B 4 C00716 AFCS SYS B ENGAGE INTLK B 10 C00207 FLIGHT CONTROL STAB TRIM CONT C 1 C01037 AFCS SYS B MACH TRIM AC C 2 C01042 AFCS SYS B SNSR EXC AC C 3 C01047 AFCS MCP DC 2 D 10 C00840 FLIGHT CONTROL STAB TRIM ACTUATOR SUBTASK 22-11-26-860-039 (15) Remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name D 2 C01045 AFCS SYS A FCC DC F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name B 3 C01046 AFCS SYS B FCC DC SUBTASK 22-11-26-790-001 (16) Do a hydraulic leak check: WARNING KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT AWAY FROM THE FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES. THE AILERONS, ELEVATORS, RUDDER, FLAPS, SLATS, SPOILERS, STABILIZER, AND NOSE GEAR CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (a) Supply hydraulic pressure to the elevator hydraulic systems A and B (TASK 27-31-00-800-801). (b) Visually examine the autopilot elevator actuator [1]. 1) Make sure that there is no hydraulic leak. (c) Remove Hydraulic power from hydraulic systems A and B, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805. PUSH <CONTINUE BEFORE YOU COMPLETE THE ROD ADJUSTMENTS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE ROD ASSEMBLIES. a) Test 51.06, ELEV LVDT (VAC), Limits: -2.05 to -1.95 NOTE: Use this CDU display to do the adjustment for the rod assemblies. THE A/P ACTUATORS, ROD ASSEMBLIES AND FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES CAN MOVE WHEN YOU PUSH THE LSK THAT IS ADJACENT TO <CONTINUE. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (6) Adjust the rod assembly [8]: (a) Adjust the length of the rod assembly [8] until the bolt [2] can go smoothly through the rod end and the autopilot elevator actuator B lever assembly [1]. NOTE: Use the CDU display (Test 51.06) to do the adjustment for the rod assembly. 1) Make sure that the elevator A/P actuator LVDT voltage is -2.00 (±0.05) VAC. 2) Make sure that you can see the threads of the rod end through the inspection hole at the end of the rod assembly [8]. 3) Adjust the rod assembly [8] if it is necessary. NOTE: The nominal length of the rod assembly is 9.43 in. (239.52 mm). (b) Tighten the locknut on the rod end. 1) Do this task: Lockwire, Cotter Pins, and Lockrings - Installation, TASK 20-10-44-400-801. (c) Install the bolt [2], washers [3], [4] and nut [5]. NOTE: The bolt must go smoothly through the rod end and the lever assembly. SUBTASK 22-11-26-420-009 WARNING DO NOT PUSH THE LSK THAT IS ADJACENT TO <CONTINUE ON TEST 51.06 WHEN YOU ADJUST THE ROD ASSEMBLIES. THE A/P ACTUATORS, ROD ASSEMBLIES AND FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES CAN MOVE WHEN YOU PUSH THE LSK THAT IS ADJACENT TO <CONTINUE. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (7) Adjust the rod assembly [6]: (a) Jiggle the aft quadrant. 1) Make sure that the trailing edge of the right elevator aligns with the index mark on the tail cone within ±0.06 inch. (b) Adjust the length of the rod assembly [6] until the bolt [2] can go smoothly through the rod and the autopilot elevator actuator A lever assembly [7]. NOTE: Use the CDU display (Test 51.06) to do the adjustment for the rod assembly. 1) Make sure that the elevator A/P actuator LVDT voltage is -2.00 (±0.05) VAC. 22-11-26 2) Make sure that you can see the threads of the rod end through the inspection hole at the end of the rod assembly [6]. 3) Adjust the rod assembly if it is necessary. NOTE: The nominal length of the rod assembly is 17.52 in. (445.01 mm). (c) Tighten the locknut on the rod end. (d) Install the bolt [2], washers [3], [4] and nut [5]. NOTE: The bolt must go smoothly through the rod end and the lever assembly. SUBTASK 22-11-26-740-001 WARNING KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT AWAY FROM THE A/P ACTUATORS, ROD ASSEMBLIES AND FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES. THE A/P ACTUATORS, ROD ASSEMBLIES AND FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES CAN MOVE WHEN YOU PUSH THE LSK THAT IS ADJACENT TO <CONTINUE. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (8) Push the LSK that is adjacent to <CONTINUE (on the CDU display - Test 51.06). (a) Do the instructions that show on the CDU display to complete the ELEV RIG test. (b) Make sure that the values for the A side and B side are between the limits that show on the CDU display.

D. Autopilot Elevator Actuator Test

SUBTASK 22-11-26-740-002 (1) Do this Built-In-Test Equipment (BITE) test: (a) Push the INIT REF key on the Control Display Unit (CDU) keyboard. (b) Push the Line Select Key (LSK) that is adjacent to each selection: NOTE: If the CONTINUE shows during the BITE test, then do the instructions that show on the CDU display before you push the LSK that is adjacent to CONTINUE. Use the NEXT PAGE or PREV PAGE key to change page if it is necessary. 22-11-26 1) INDEX 2) MAINT 3) DFCS 4) EXTENDED MAINTENANCE 5) BITE LIBRARY TEST 6) Make a selection for the applicable channel: NOTE: If you do the test as a scheduled maintenance task, you must do the CHANNEL A test, the CHANNEL B test, and the CHANNEL A AND B test. NOTE: A/P (Autopilot) elevator actuator A has interface with the Flight Control Computer (FCC) A (Channel A). A/P elevator actuator B has interface with the FCC B (Channel B). a) CHANNEL A b) CHANNEL B c) CHANNEL A AND B 7) RUN SELECT LIBRARY TESTS 8) 30 ELEV 9) EXECUTE 10) Do the instructions that show on the CDU display to complete the test. RYR 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020; AIRPLANES WITH HONEYWELL FCC HARDWARE INSTALLED NOTE: If the test of the library 60.30 (30 ELEVATOR) shows “TEST FAILED” at step S053, but the fail values on the CDU are between the expanded limits (-2.88, -2.10) and the remainder of the test passes, then the full test is a TEST PASS. NOTE: If the system continues to fail with expanded limits, it is necessary to check the friction in the elevator cable system, including all pulleys. Also it is necessary to check the spring force of the springs within the feel of centering (TASK 27-31-64-400-802). RYR ALL 11) Make sure that the test is completed with no failure or the "TEST FAILED" message does not show.

22-11-26-200-802Autopilot Elevator Actuator Linkage Inspection ATA 22 · Task 200-802

Task Description

2. Autopilot Elevator Actuator Linkage Inspection (Figure 601 and Figure 602)

A. General

(1) To do the inspection, it is necessary to remove the autopilot elevator actuator linkages. Usually this task is used to do the overhaul of the autopilot elevator actuator linkages. To get access to the components or replace the components during the inspection, do this task: Autopilot Elevator Actuator - Removal, TASK 22-11-26-000-801.

B. References

Reference Title 22-11-26-000-801 Autopilot Elevator Actuator - Removal (P/B 401)

C. Tools/Equipment

Reference Description STD-1096 Micrometer - Depth, 0-1 inch, Readable to 1/1000 inch STD-1097 Caliper - Vernier, 0-6 inch, Readable to 1/1000 inch

D. Autopilot Elevator Actuator Linkage Inspection

SUBTASK 22-11-26-200-008 (1) Do a visual check of the both lever assemblies while connected to the autopilot elevator actuators output shafts (Views D and E, Figure 601). (a) Manually move each lever assembly. 1) Make sure that the lever assemblies do not have looseness/freeplay while connected to the autopilot elevator actuator. NOTE: If looseness/freeplay is present, the lever arm will move sideways, along the direction of the autopilot elevator output shaft. (b) If lever assemblies have looseness/freeplay, do the following steps: 1) Tighten the lever assembly nut [9] to 34 ±1 in-lb (3.8 ±0.1 N·m). a) Make sure that the looseness/freeplay is no longer present. 2) If the looseness/freeplay is still present, replace the lever assembly. a) Make sure that the looseness is no longer present. SUBTASK 22-11-26-020-008 (2) Remove the parts that are necessary for inspection (Figure 601). SUBTASK 22-11-26-200-003 (3) Examine the removed parts as follows: (a) Use a micrometer (0-1 inch, readable to 1/1000 inch), STD-1096, or a vernier caliper (0 - 6 inch, readable to 1/1000 inch), STD-1097, to measure the parts. (b) Compare the dimensions you measured with the permitted dimensions (Figure 602). 22-11-26 (c) Repair or replace the parts that are out of the tolerance. SUBTASK 22-11-26-420-010 (4) Install the parts (Figure 601).
