22-11-27-820-801Spoiler Position Sensor Adjustment ATA 22 · Task 820-801

Task Description

2. Spoiler Position Sensor Adjustment (Figure 501)

A. References

Reference Title 20-10-44-000-801 Lockwire, Cotter Pins, and Lockrings - Removal (P/B 401) 20-10-44-400-801 Lockwire, Cotter Pins, and Lockrings - Installation (P/B 401) 22-11-00-820-803 Aileron Rigging Test (P/B 501) 27-51-00-860-803 Extend the Trailing Edge Flaps (P/B 201) 27-51-00-860-804 Retract the Trailing Edge Flaps (P/B 201) 29-11-00-860-801 Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization (P/B 201) 29-11-00-860-805 Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal (P/B 201)

B. Location Zones

Zone Area 211 Flight Compartment - Left 212 Flight Compartment - Right 563 Left Wing - Spoiler No. 4 663 Right Wing - Spoiler No. 9

C. Prepare for the Adjustment

SUBTASK 22-11-27-860-041 (1) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3 Row Col Number Name D 18 C00451 LANDING GEAR AURAL WARN SUBTASK 22-11-27-860-014 WARNING KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT AWAY FROM THE FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES. THE AILERONS, THE ELEVATORS, THE RUDDER, THE FLAPS, THE SLATS, THE SPOILERS, THE STABILIZER AND THE NOSE GEAR CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (2) Supply hydraulic power to hydraulic systems A and B (TASK 29-11-00-860-801). 22-11-27 SUBTASK 22-11-27-860-015 (3) Do this task: Extend the Trailing Edge Flaps, TASK 27-51-00-860-803. SUBTASK 22-11-27-860-016 (4) Set the speedbrake control lever to the DOWN position. SUBTASK 22-11-27-860-017 (5) Set the aileron trim to zero. SUBTASK 22-11-27-860-018 (6) Put the pilot's control wheel in the center position. (a) Jiggle the pilot's control wheel. (b) Make sure that the pilot's control wheel is in the center position. SUBTASK 22-11-27-860-019 (7) Set the autopilot stab trim cutout switch, on the control stand, to the CUTOUT position. SUBTASK 22-11-27-860-020 (8) Make sure that the VHF NAV and IRS switches, on the P5 forward overhead panel, are in the NORMAL positions. SUBTASK 22-11-27-860-021 (9) Set the left and right IRS select switches, on the P5 aft overhead panel, to the ALIGN or NAV position.

D. Procedure

NOTE: Two persons are necessary for this task. SUBTASK 22-11-27-820-003 (1) Do this BITE test: (a) Push the INIT REF key on the Control Display Unit (CDU) keyboard. (b) Push the Line Select Key (LSK) that is adjacent to each selection: NOTE: If the CONTINUE shows during the BITE test, then do the instructions that show on the CDU display before you push the LSK that is adjacent to CONTINUE. Use the NEXT PAGE or PREV PAGE key to change page if it is necessary. 1) INDEX 2) MAINT 3) DFCS 4) EXTENDED MAINTENANCE 5) RIGGING 6) AILERON 7) SPOILER. (c) Do the instructions that show on the CDU display until test 52.23. NOTE: For detailed data about the SPOILER test, refer to "Do the Spoiler Check" in (TASK 22-11-00-820-803). (d) Make sure that the values for the A side and B side are between the limits that show on the CDU display. 1) Test 52.23, SPOILER 4 (VAC), Limits: -0.20 to +0.20 NOTE: Use this CDU display to do the adjustment for the spoiler position sensor (No. 4). 22-11-27 WARNING DO NOT PUSH THE LSK WHEN YOU ADJUST THE SPOILER POSITION SENSOR. THE AILERONS, SPOILERS AND FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES CAN MOVE WHEN YOU PUSH THE LSK. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (e) Adjust the spoiler position sensor (No. 4): 1) Loosen the bolt [1] on the mounting bracket until you can turn the spoiler position sensor. NOTE: You do not have to remove the bolt, washers, and nut. 2) Turn the spoiler position sensor until you get a value less than 0.10 VAC. 3) Tighten the bolt [1] on the mounting bracket to 35 in-lb (4 N·m). 4) Do this check: a) Slowly move the speedbrake lever aft and look at the CDU display while the spoilers start to move up. b) If the value on the CDU decreases toward zero before it increases when the speed brake starts to move up, then do these steps: c) Put the speedbrake lever to the DOWN position. d) Do the above adjustment for the spoiler position sensor (No. 4) again. e) If the value on the CDU does not decrease toward zero before it increases when the speedbrake starts to move up, then continue. f) Remove the lockwire from the thumbnut on the micro-adjustment rod (TASK 20-10-44-000-801). g) Turn the thumbnut on the micro-adjustment rod until you get a smallest possible value less than 0.06 VAC. h) Install lockwire on the thumbnut (TASK 20-10-44-400-801). WARNING DO NOT PUSH THE LSK WHEN YOU ADJUST THE SPOILER POSITION SENSOR. THE AILERONS, SPOILERS AND FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES CAN MOVE WHEN YOU PUSH THE LSK. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . i) Push the LSK that is adjacent to <CONTINUE. j) Test 52.24, SPOILER 9 (VAC), Limits: -0.20 to +0.20 NOTE: Use this CDU display to do the adjustment for the spoiler position sensor (No. 9). WARNING DO NOT PUSH THE LSK WHEN YOU ADJUST THE SPOILER POSITION SENSOR. THE AILERONS, SPOILERS AND FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES CAN MOVE WHEN YOU PUSH THE LSK. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (f) Adjust the spoiler position sensor (No. 9): 1) Loosen the bolt [1] on the mounting bracket until you can turn the spoiler position sensor. NOTE: You do not have to remove the bolt, washers, and nut. 2) Turn the spoiler position sensor until you get a value less than 0.10 VAC. 22-11-27 3) Tighten the bolt [1] on the mounting bracket to 35 in-lb (4 N·m). 4) Do this check: a) Slowly move the speedbrake lever aft and look at the CDU display while the spoilers start to move up. b) If the value on the CDU decreases toward zero before it increases when the speed brake starts to move up, then do these steps: c) Put the speedbrake lever to the DOWN position. d) Do the above adjustment for the spoiler position sensor (No. 9) again. e) If the value on the CDU does not decrease toward zero before it increases when the speed brake starts to move up, then continue. f) Remove the lockwire from the thumbnut on the micro-adjustment rod (TASK 20-10-44-000-801). g) Turn the thumbnut on the micro-adjustment rod until you get a smallest possible value less than 0.06 VAC. h) Install lockwire on the thumbnut (TASK 20-10-44-400-801). WARNING DO NOT PUSH THE LSK WHEN YOU ADJUST THE SPOILER POSITION SENSOR. THE AILERONS, SPOILERS AND FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES CAN MOVE WHEN YOU PUSH THE LSK. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . 5) Push the LSK that is adjacent to <CONTINUE (on the CDU display - Test 52.24). a) Do the instructions that show on the CDU display to complete the SPOILER test. b) Make sure that the values for the A side and B side are between the limits that show on the CDU display.

E. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 22-11-27-860-022 (1) Push the captain's or first officer's autopilot disengage switch, on the control wheel, to make sure that the autopilot is disengaged. SUBTASK 22-11-27-860-038 (2) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3 Row Col Number Name D 18 C00451 LANDING GEAR AURAL WARN SUBTASK 22-11-27-860-024 (3) Set the autopilot stab trim cutout switch, on the control stand, to the NORMAL position. SUBTASK 22-11-27-860-025 (4) Do this task: Retract the Trailing Edge Flaps, TASK 27-51-00-860-804. SUBTASK 22-11-27-860-026 (5) Remove hydraulic power from hydraulic systems A and B (TASK 29-11-00-860-805).

E. Aileron Position Sensor Installation

SUBTASK 22-11-29-820-002 (1) Align the reference mark on the sensor case with the reference mark on the sensor shaft. SUBTASK 22-11-29-420-001 (2) Do these steps to install the aileron position sensor [11]: (a) Put the aileron position sensor [11] into the clamp [10] and crank [9] with the zero reference alignment mark aligned with the slot in the crank [9] Figure 401. 1) Make sure that the zero reference alignment mark is oriented in the closed end direction. NOTE: If the sensor shaft and crank are not oriented correctly, it will cause the DFCS BITE aileron rigging and surface tests to fail. 2) Tighten the bolt [8] in the crank [9] to 35 in-lb (4 N·m). 3) Tighten the bolt [6] in the clamp [10] to 35 in-lb (4 N·m). SUBTASK 22-11-29-420-002 (3) Install the clamp [2] with the bolt [3], washers [4], and nut [5]. SUBTASK 22-11-29-420-003 (4) Connect the electrical connector [1]. Task Description

2. Aileron Position Sensor Adjustment (Figure 501)

A. References

Reference Title 20-10-44-000-801 Lockwire, Cotter Pins, and Lockrings - Removal (P/B 401) 20-10-44-400-801 Lockwire, Cotter Pins, and Lockrings - Installation (P/B 401) 22-11-00-820-803 Aileron Rigging Test (P/B 501) 24-22-00-860-811 Supply Electrical Power (P/B 201) 24-22-00-860-812 Remove Electrical Power (P/B 201) 29-11-00-860-801 Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization (P/B 201) 29-11-00-860-805 Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal (P/B 201) 32-00-01-480-801 Landing Gear Downlock Pins Installation (P/B 201)

B. Location Zones

Zone Area 133 Main Landing Gear Wheel Well, Body Station 663.75 to Body Station 727.00 - Left 211 Flight Compartment - Left 212 Flight Compartment - Right

C. Prepare for the Adjustment

SUBTASK 22-11-29-860-001 (1) Do this task: Supply Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-811. SUBTASK 22-11-29-860-035 (2) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3 Row Col Number Name D 18 C00451 LANDING GEAR AURAL WARN SUBTASK 22-11-29-860-002 (3) Set the autopilot stab trim cutout switch, on the control stand, to the CUTOUT position. SUBTASK 22-11-29-860-003 (4) Make sure that the VHF NAV and IRS switches, on the P5 forward overhead panel, are in the NORMAL positions. SUBTASK 22-11-29-860-004 (5) Set the left and right IRS select switches, on the P5 aft overhead panel, to the ALIGN or NAV position. 22-11-29 SUBTASK 22-11-29-860-005 WARNING KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT AWAY FROM THE FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES. THE AILERONS, THE ELEVATORS, THE RUDDER, THE FLAPS, THE SLATS, THE SPOILERS, THE STABILIZER AND THE NOSE GEAR CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (6) Supply hydraulic power to hydraulic systems A and B. To supply hydraulic power, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801. SUBTASK 22-11-29-860-006 (7) Make sure that the ailerons and the aileron trim are set to zero. SUBTASK 22-11-29-860-007 (8) Set the speed brake handle to the down position. SUBTASK 22-11-29-860-008 WARNING YOU MUST CAREFULLY INSTALL THE GROUND LOCKS IN ALL LANDING GEAR. AN ACCIDENTAL RETRACTION OF THE LANDING GEAR CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (9) Make sure that you install the landing gear downlock pins (TASK 32-00-01-480-801).

D. Procedure

NOTE: Two persons are necessary for this task. SUBTASK 22-11-29-820-001 (1) Do this BITE test: (a) Push the INIT REF key on the CDU keyboard. (b) Push the Line Select Key (LSK) that is adjacent to each selection: NOTE: If the CONTINUE shows during the BITE test, then do the instructions that show on the CDU display before you push the LSK that is adjacent to CONTINUE. Use the NEXT PAGE or PREV PAGE key to change page if it is necessary. 1) INDEX 2) MAINT 3) DFCS 4) EXTENDED MAINTENANCE 5) RIGGING 6) AILERON 7) AIL RIG 8) Do the instructions that show on the CDU display until test 52.01. NOTE: For detailed data about the AIL RIG test, refer to "Do the Aileron Rigging Check" in (TASK 22-11-00-820-803). 9) Make sure that the values for the A side and B side are between the limits that show on the CDU display. a) Test 52.01, AIL POS (VAC), Limits: -0.06 to +0.06 NOTE: Use this CDU display to do the adjustment for the aileron position sensor. 22-11-29 WARNING DO NOT SELECT <CONTINUE ON TEST 52.01 OR TEST 51.01 WHEN YOU ADJUST THE SENSOR. THE FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES CAN MOVE WHEN YOU PUSH THE LSK NEXT TO <CONTINUE. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . 10) Adjust the aileron position sensor: a) Loosen the bolt [1] on the clamp until you can turn the aileron position sensor. NOTE: You do not have to remove the bolt [1], washer [2] and nut [3]. b) Turn the aileron position sensor slowly in the clockwise and counter-clockwise directions until you get a value less than 0.06 VAC. c) Tighten the bolt [1] on the clamp to 35 in-lb (4 N·m). d) Remove the lockwire on the thumb nut on the micro-adjustment rod (TASK 20-10-44-000-801). e) Turn the thumb nut on the micro-adjustment rod until you get a smallest value less than 0.03 VAC. f) Install the lockwire on the thumb nut on the micro-adjustment rod (TASK 20-10-44-400-801). WARNING KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT AWAY FROM THE AILERON POSITION SENSOR AND FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES. THESE PARTS CAN MOVE WHEN YOU PUSH THE LSK NEXT TO <CONTINUE. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . 11) Push the LSK that is adjacent to <CONTINUE (on the CDU display - Test 52.01). 12) Do the instructions that show on the CDU display to complete the AIL RIG test. 13) Make sure that the values for the A side and B side are between the limits that show on the CDU display.

E. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 22-11-29-860-009 (1) Push the captain's or first officer's autopilot disengage switch on the control wheel to make sure that the autopilot is disengaged. SUBTASK 22-11-29-860-032 (2) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3 Row Col Number Name D 18 C00451 LANDING GEAR AURAL WARN SUBTASK 22-11-29-860-011 (3) Set the autopilot stab trim cutout switch, on the control stand, to the NORMAL position. SUBTASK 22-11-29-860-012 (4) Remove hydraulic power from hydraulic systems A and B. To remove hydraulic power, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805. 22-11-29 SUBTASK 22-11-29-860-013 (5) Do this task: Remove Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-812.

H. Elevator Position Sensor Installation

SUBTASK 22-11-30-820-002 (1) Align the reference mark on the sensor case with the reference mark on the sensor shaft. SUBTASK 22-11-30-420-001 (2) Install the elevator position sensor [6]. (a) Put the elevator position sensor [6] into the bracket and the crank [5] with the zero reference alignment mark aligned with the slot in the crank [5]. G. Stabilizer Position Sensor Installation

SUBTASK 22-11-31-820-002 (1) Align the reference mark on the sensor case with the reference mark on the bracket. E. Prepare for the Adjustment

SUBTASK 22-11-31-860-001 (1) Do this task: Supply Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-811. SUBTASK 22-11-31-860-026 (2) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3 Row Col Number Name D 18 C00451 LANDING GEAR AURAL WARN SUBTASK 22-11-31-010-001 (3) To get access to the stabilizer position sensors, remove this access door: Number Name/Location 318BR T ailcone Access Door SUBTASK 22-11-31-010-002 (4) To get access to the stabilizer trim jackscrew, open this access door: Number Name/Location 311BL Stabilizer Trim Access Door SUBTASK 22-11-31-980-001 (5) Do these steps to set the B dimension (Figure 502): NOTE: The B dimension is measured between the center of the upper and lower Gimbal pins on the stabilizer trim jackscrew. To do this, one person must be in the tail of the airplane with a headset and the other person in the flight compartment (a) Turn the stab trim wheel handle on the control stand to set the B dimension. NOTE: This B dimension is equivalent to the horizontal stabilizer at 4 units of trim (zero degree). (b) Use the trammel trammel bar, SPL-1677, to measure the B dimension. 1) Make sure that the B dimension is 39.89 ±0.01 in. (1013.21 ±0.26 mm). SUBTASK 22-11-31-860-002 (6) Set the autopilot stab trim cutout switch, on the control stand, to the CUTOUT position. SUBTASK 22-11-31-860-003 (7) Make sure that the VHF NAV and IRS switches, on the P5 forward overhead panel, are in the NORMAL positions. SUBTASK 22-11-31-860-004 (8) Set the left and right IRS select switches, on the P5 aft overhead panel, to the ALIGN or NAV position. 22-11-31 SUBTASK 22-11-31-860-005 WARNING KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT AWAY FROM THE FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES. THE AILERONS, ELEVATORS, RUDDER, FLAPS, SLATS, SPOILERS, STABILIZER AND NOSE GEAR CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (9) Supply hydraulic power to hydraulic systems A and B. To supply hydraulic power, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801. F. Procedure NOTE: Two persons are necessary for this task. SUBTASK 22-11-31-820-001 (1) Do this BITE test: (a) Push the INIT REF key on the CDU keyboard. (b) Push the Line Select Key (LSK) that is adjacent to each selection: NOTE: If the CONTINUE shows during the BITE test, then do the instructions that show on the CDU display before you push the LSK that is adjacent to CONTINUE. Use the NEXT PAGE or PREV PAGE key to change page if it is necessary. 1) INDEX 2) MAINT 3) DFCS 4) EXTENDED MAINTENANCE 5) RIGGING 6) STABILIZER 7) Do the instructions that show on the CDU display until test 54.01. NOTE: Use the trammel trammel bar, SPL-1677 for measurement of the "B" dimension that shows on the CDU display (Test 54.01). NOTE: For detailed data about the STAB RIG test, refer to Stabilizer Rigging Test, TASK 22-11-00-820-805. a) Test 54.01, STAB POS (VAC), Limits: -0.07 to +0.07 NOTE: Use this CDU display to do the adjustment for the stabilizer position sensors. b) Jiggle the aft quadrant. c) Make sure that the right elevator trailing edge aligns with the elevator index on the tail cone at 0 ±0.06 inch. WARNING DO NOT PUSH THE LSK THAT IS ADJACENT TO <CONTINUE ON TEST 54.01 WHEN YOU ADJUST THE STABILIZER POSITION SENSOR. THE ACTUATORS, ROD ASSEMBLIES AND FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES CAN MOVE WHEN YOU PUSH THE LSK THAT IS ADJACENT TO <CONTINUE. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . 8) Adjust the stabilizer position sensor A [4]: 22-11-31 a) Loosen the bolt [1] on the bracket until you can turn the stabilizer position sensor. NOTE: You do not have to remove the bolt [1], washer [2] and nut [3]. b) Turn the stabilizer position sensor slowly in the clockwise and counter-clockwise directions until the voltage is less than 0.0 ±0.5 VAC. c) Tighten the bolt [1] on the bracket to 35 in-lb (4 N·m) . d) Remove the lockwire on the micro-adjustment nut (TASK 20-10-44-000-801). e) Turn the micro-adjustment nut until you get a smallest possible voltage that is between -0.07 and +0.07 VAC. f) Install the lockwire on the micro-adjustment nut (TASK 20-10-44-400-801). WARNING DO NOT PUSH THE LSK THAT IS ADJACENT TO <CONTINUE ON TEST 51.01 WHEN YOU ADJUST THE STABILIZER POSITION SENSOR. THE ACTUATORS, ROD ASSEMBLIES AND FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES CAN MOVE WHEN YOU PUSH THE LSK THAT IS ADJACENT TO <CONTINUE. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . 9) Adjust the stabilizer position sensor B [5]: a) Loosen the bolt [1] on the bracket until you can turn the stabilizer position sensor. NOTE: You do not have to remove the bolt [1], washer [2] and nut [3]. b) Turn the stabilizer position sensor slowly in the clockwise and counter-clockwise directions until the voltage is less than 0.0 ±0.5 VAC. c) Tighten the bolt [1] on the bracket to 35 in-lb (4 N·m). d) Remove the lockwire on the micro-adjustment nut (TASK 20-10-44-000-801). e) Turn the micro-adjustment nut until you get a smallest possible voltage that is between -0.07 and +0.07 VAC. f) Install the lockwire on the micro-adjustment nut (TASK 20-10-44-400-801). WARNING KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT AWAY FROM THE STABILIZER POSITION SENSOR. THE ACTUATORS, ROD ASSEMBLIES AND FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES CAN MOVE WHEN YOU PUSH THE LSK THAT IS ADJACENT TO <CONTINUE. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (c) Push the LSK that is adjacent to <CONTINUE (on the CDU display - Test 54.01). 1) Do the instructions that show on the CDU display to complete the STAB RIG test. 2) Make sure that the values for the A side and B side are between the limits that show on the CDU display.

22-11-33-470-820FCC Software Installation from the Flight Compartment with a Portable Data Loader ATA 22 · Task 470-820

Task Description

4. FCC Software Installation from the Flight Compartment with a Portable Data Loader

A. General

(1) This procedure tells you how to install Operational Program Software (OPS) in the Flight Control Computer (FCC). (2) A portable data loader (PDL) is necessary for this procedure. A data loader control panel and a PDL interface connector are also necessary. There must be an FCC switch position on the data loader control panel. The data loader control panel is installed above the DATA TRANSFER UNIT RECEPTACLE connector on the P61 panel. (3) A PDL is not a Boeing supplied part. Refer to the PDL supplier for instructions for operation. PDLs have a disk drive for software installation from disks. Some PDLs have an internal mass storage device. If the software is stored in the PDL, then disks are not necessary. (4) The airplane must be on the ground with the engines shutdown before you can install software. (5) Modern software loaders that meet the security requirements defined in ARINC 645-1 or newer are recommended to use. The procedures for modern software loaders will be marked as preferred for now and will be the only procedures available after removing floppy disk loaders procedures in the future. Please check with your Software Loader Supplier for current capabilities since this is still maturing across current and future software loaders.

B. References

Reference Title 20-15-11-400-801 On-Airplane Software - Installation (P/B 201)

C. Tools/Equipment

NOTE: When more than one tool part number is listed under the same "Reference" number, the tools shown are alternates to each other within the same airplane series. Tool part numbers that are replaced or non-procurable are preceded by "Opt:", which stands for Optional. 22-11-33 Reference Description COM-1915 Data Loader - ARINC 615 (without ARINC 645-1 Compliant) Part #: 11615-50 Supplier: 0D4J3 Part #: 2231560-1-B Supplier: 98571 Part #: 465130-01-01 Supplier: 30782 Part #: 800-0631 Supplier: 1JSZ6 Part #: CEI-715-DL-2 Supplier: 0BPH5 Part #: PXS-LDS-10 Supplier: 98571 Part #: YV68A110 Supplier: FAQ15 Opt Part #: 11615-02 Supplier: 0D4J3 Opt Part #: 11615-20 Supplier: 0D4J3 Opt Part #: 18000-02 Supplier: 0D4J3 Opt Part #: 30100 Supplier: 0BAW0 Opt Part #: 80000-03-01010203 Supplier: 0BAW0 Opt Part #: 80000-04-01020301 Supplier: 0BAW0 Opt Part #: 80000-05 Supplier: 0BAW0 Opt Part #: 964-0400-020 Supplier: 97896 Opt Part #: 964-0400-024 Supplier: 97896 Opt Part #: 964-0400-025 Supplier: 97896 Opt Part #: 964-0400-030 Supplier: 97896 Opt Part #: 964-0400-044 Supplier: 97896 Opt Part #: 964-0400-045 Supplier: 97896 Opt Part #: 964-0400-050 Supplier: 97896 Opt Part #: 964-0400-054 Supplier: 97896 Opt Part #: 964-0400-055 Supplier: 97896 Opt Part #: P2K-615A-06 Supplier: 0BAW0 COM-21223 Data Loader - ARINC 615 (with ARINC 645-1 Compliant) Part #: 403474 Supplier: CG603 Part #: 403562 Supplier: CG603 Part #: AE-615-MPDL Supplier: CD624 Part #: AE-DL-SMD Supplier: CD624 Part #: PDL-615-XT Supplier: 89Q20 Part #: PXS-LDS-12 Supplier: 98571

(a) Set the power switch on the portable data loader to the on position. (b) Put the correct disk in the disk drive. (c) Follow the prompts on the data loader to complete the installation. NOTE: COMP , LOAD COMPLETE and TRANSF COMPLETE are examples of data loader prompts for a completed installation. (d) Remove the disk from the disk drive. SUBTASK 22-11-33-940-002 CAUTION SET THE POWER SWITCH FOR THE PORTABLE DATA LOADER TO OFF BEFORE YOU CONNECT , OR REMOVE THE INTERFACE CABLE. IF THE POWER SWITCH IS NOT OFF , DAMAGE TO THE PORTABLE DATA LOADER CAN OCCUR. (8) Set the power switch on the data loader to the off position. SUBTASK 22-11-33-860-170 (9) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name D 2 C01045 AFCS SYS A FCC DC SUBTASK 22-11-33-860-051 (10) Remove the interface cable from the DATA TRANSFER UNIT RECEPTACLE on the P61 panel. 22-11-33 SUBTASK 22-11-33-860-057 (11) After two minutes, do the Software Installation Test below.

I. Software Installation Test from the FMCS CDU

SUBTASK 22-11-33-420-010 (1) Do these steps to test the software installation: (a) If you are not at one of the DFCS BITE TEST displays, then do these steps: 1) Push the INIT REF function key. 2) If the POS INIT display shows, then push the line select key adjacent to the INDEX prompt. NOTE: This makes the INIT/REF INDEX show. 3) Push the line select key adjacent to the MAINT prompt. (b) From the MAINT BITE INDEX, push the line select key adjacent to the DFCS prompt. NOTE: The DFCS will do a self-test. (c) When the self-test is complete, push the line select key adjacent to the IDENTIFICATION AND CONFIGURATION prompt. (d) Push the line select key adjacent to the CHANNEL A prompt. 1) Make sure that the software part number for FCC A is correct. NOTE: The software part number shows below FCC OPS. NOTE: Refer to the Expendables/Parts table for FCC OPS [1]. (e) Push the line select key adjacent to the PREV MENU prompt. (f) Push the line select key adjacent to the CHANNEL B prompt. 1) Make sure that the software part number for FCC B is correct. NOTE: The software part number shows below FCC OPS. NOTE: Refer to the Expendables/Parts table for FCC OPS [1]. (g) Push the line select key adjacent to the PREV MENU prompt. (h) Push the line select key adjacent to the PREV MENU prompt. (i) Push the line select key adjacent to the FAULT REVIEW prompt. (j) Push the line select key adjacent to the ERASE FAULT HISTORY prompt. (k) Push the line select key adjacent to the CHANNEL A AND B prompt. (l) Push the line select key adjacent to the YES prompt. (m) Push and release the line select key adjacent to the EXIT prompt until you are out of DFCS BITE.

22-11-33-470-821FCC Inflight Faults Memory Download with a Portable Data Loader ATA 22 · Task 470-821

Task Description

5. FCC Inflight Faults Memory Download with a Portable Data Loader

A. General

(1) This procedure tells you how to download Flights Faults Memory in the FCC. (2) A portable data loader (PDL) is necessary for this procedure. A data loader panel and a PDL interface connector cable are also necessary. There must be an FCC switch position on the data loader selector panel. The data loader selector switch is installed above the DATA TRANSFER UNIT RECEPTACLE connector on the (P61) panel. The PDL interface connector cable is hooked up to the data transfer unit receptacle connector for this procedure. (3) The airplane must be on the ground with the engines shutdown before you can download the FCC flight faults memory. (4) Modern software loaders that meet the security requirements defined in ARINC 645-1 or newer are recommended to use. The procedures for modern software loaders will be marked as preferred for now and will be the only procedures available after removing floppy disk loaders procedures in the future. Please check with your Software Loader Supplier for current capabilities since this is still maturing across current and future software loaders.

B. Tools/Equipment

22-11-33-470-822FCC BITE Test Data Download from the Flight Compartment with a Portable Data Loader ATA 22 · Task 470-822

Task Description

6. FCC BITE Test Data Download from the Flight Compartment with a Portable Data Loader

A. General

(1) This procedure tells you how to download Flights Faults Memory in the FCC. (2) A portable data loader (PDL) is necessary for this procedure. A data loader control panel and a PDL interface connector are also necessary. There must be an FCC switch position on the data loader control panel. The data loader control panel is installed above the DATA TRANSFER UNIT RECEPTACLE connector on the (P61) panel. (3) The airplane must be on the ground with the engines shutdown before you can install software. (4) Modern software loaders that meet the security requirements defined in ARINC 645-1 or newer are recommended to use. The procedures for modern software loaders will be marked as preferred for now and will be the only procedures available after removing floppy disk loaders procedures in the future. Please check with your Software Loader Supplier for current capabilities since this is still maturing across current and future software loaders.

B. Tools/Equipment

NOTE: When more than one tool part number is listed under the same "Reference" number, the tools shown are alternates to each other within the same airplane series. Tool part numbers that are replaced or non-procurable are preceded by "Opt:", which stands for Optional. 22-11-33-470-823FCC Software Installation from the Electrical and Electronics Compartment with a Portable Data ATA 22 · Task 470-823

Task Description

7. FCC Software Installation from the Electrical and Electronics Compartment with a Portable Data Loader

A. General

(1) This procedure tells you how to install Operational Program Software (OPS) in the Flight Control Computer (FCC). (2) A portable data loader (PDL) is necessary for this procedure. (3) The airplane must be on the ground with the engines shutdown before you can install software. (4) Modern software loaders that meet the security requirements defined in ARINC 645-1 or newer are recommended to use. The procedures for modern software loaders will be marked as preferred for now and will be the only procedures available after removing floppy disk loaders procedures in the future. Please check with your Software Loader Supplier for current capabilities since this is still maturing across current and future software loaders. 22-11-33

NOTE: COMP , LOAD COMPLETE and TRANSF COMPLETE are examples of data loader prompts for a completed installation. (d) Remove the disk from the disk drive when the software installation is completed. 22-11-33-470-824FCC Software Installation using the Cross-load Function ATA 22 · Task 470-824

Task Description

8. FCC Software Installation using the Cross-load Function

A. General

(1) This procedure tells you how to install Operational Program Software (OPS) from one Flight Control Computer (FCC) to the other FCC. (2) The airplane must be on the ground with the engines shutdown before you can cross-load software.

B. Expendables/Parts

C. Location Zones

Zone Area 212 Flight Compartment - Right 22-11-33 RYR 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999; RYR 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020 WITH COLLINS E-FCC SOFTWARE P8.0 OR WITH COLLINS E-FCC SOFTWARE P9.0 OR WITH COLLINS E-FCC SOFTWARE P11.1 (Continued)

D. FCC Cross-load Software Installation Procedure

SUBTASK 22-11-33-860-060 (1) Make sure the DFCS is not engaged. SUBTASK 22-11-33-860-061 (2) Use the cross-load function to install software in the FCC. NOTE: For the FCC to be an approved installation, the correct FCC OPS must be installed. Refer to the Expendables/Parts table for FCC OPS [1]. SUBTASK 22-11-33-860-062 (3) Make sure that these circuit breakers are closed: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name D 2 C01045 AFCS SYS A FCC DC F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name B 3 C01046 AFCS SYS B FCC DC SUBTASK 22-11-33-860-063 (4) Do these steps to install the software into an FCC: (a) On the FMCS CDU, if you are not at one of the DFCS BITE TEST displays, then do these steps: 1) Push the INIT REF function key. 2) If the POS INIT display shows, then push the line select key adjacent to the INDEX prompt. NOTE: This makes the INIT/REF INDEX show. 3) Push the line select key adjacent to the MAINT prompt. (b) From the MAINT BITE INDEX, push the line select key adjacent to the DFCS prompt. NOTE: The DFCS will do a self-test. (c) When the self-test is complete, push the line select key adjacent to the IDENTIFICATION AND CONFIGURATION prompt. (d) Push the line select key adjacent to the CROSSLOAD prompt. NOTE: The CROSSLOAD prompt only appears if the FCCs have different OPS part numbers installed. The OPS and OPC software part numbers will be displayed for both FCC-A and FCC-B. (e) To load software from FCC-A to FCC-B, push the line select key adjacent to the A TO B prompt. (f) To load software from FCC-B to FCC-A, push the line select key adjacent to the B TO A prompt. (g) To start the software cross-load, push the line select key adjacent to the YES prompt. (h) If the software cross-load is successful, the following BITE screen will be displayed: 22-11-33 RYR 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999; RYR 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020 WITH COLLINS E-FCC SOFTWARE P8.0 OR WITH COLLINS E-FCC SOFTWARE P9.0 OR WITH COLLINS E-FCC SOFTWARE P11.1 (Continued) DFCS BITE TEST CROSSLOAD FROM FCC-A (or B) CROSSLOAD COMPLETE. INITIALIZATION OF FCC IN PROGRESS. THIS MAY REQUIRE 30 SECONDS. NOTE: The software cross-load may take between 6 and 8 minutes. During this time the message IN PROGRESS will be displayed. SUBTASK 22-11-33-860-064 (5) After two minutes, do the Software Installation Test below. If cross-loading is successful, the CDU should display the DFCS BITE TEST MAIN MENU.

E. Software Installation Test from the FMCS CDU

SUBTASK 22-11-33-420-011 (1) Do these steps to test the software installation: (a) If you are not at one of the DFCS BITE TEST displays, then do these steps: 1) Push the INIT REF function key. 2) If the POS INIT display shows, then push the line select key adjacent to the INDEX prompt. NOTE: This makes the INIT/REF INDEX show. 3) Push the line select key adjacent to the MAINT prompt. (b) From the MAINT BITE INDEX, push the line select key adjacent to the DFCS prompt. NOTE: The DFCS will do a self-test. (c) When the self-test is complete, push the line select key adjacent to the IDENTIFICATION AND CONFIGURATION prompt. (d) Push the line select key adjacent to the CHANNEL A prompt. 1) Make sure that the software part number for FCC A is correct. NOTE: The software part number shows below FCC OPS. NOTE: Refer to the Expendables/Parts table for FCC OPS [1]. (e) Push the line select key adjacent to the PREV MENU prompt. (f) Push the line select key adjacent to the CHANNEL B prompt. 1) Make sure that the software part number for FCC B is correct. NOTE: The software part number shows below FCC OPS. NOTE: Refer to the Expendables/Parts table for FCC OPS [1]. (g) Push the line select key adjacent to the PREV MENU prompt. (h) Push the line select key adjacent to the PREV MENU prompt. (i) Push the line select key adjacent to the FAULT REVIEW prompt. (j) Push the line select key adjacent to the ERASE FAULT HISTORY prompt. 22-11-33 RYR 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999; RYR 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020 WITH COLLINS E-FCC SOFTWARE P8.0 OR WITH COLLINS E-FCC SOFTWARE P9.0 OR WITH COLLINS E-FCC SOFTWARE P11.1 (Continued) (k) Push the line select key adjacent to the CHANNEL A AND B prompt. (l) Push the line select key adjacent to the YES prompt. (m) Push and release the line select key adjacent to the EXIT prompt until you are out of DFCS BITE.

SUBTASK 22-11-33-740-002 (2) Do these steps to make sure that the hardware and software are correct: NOTE: For the FCC to be an approved installation, the correct FCC and FCC Operational Program Software (OPS) must be installed. (b) Push the line select key next to the IDENTIFICATION AND CONFIGURATION prompt. (c) Push the line select key next to the CHANNEL A prompt. 1) Make sure that the HARDWARE PART NUMBER and FCC OPS for channel A are correct. a) If the FCC OPS part number is not correct, load the correct software (TASK 22-11-33-470-823 or TASK 22-11-33-470-820 or TASK 22-11-33-470-824). NOTE: AIRPLANES WITH COLLINS FCCs; 22-11-33 If the correct software part number is installed on FCC-A, it may be cross-loaded to FCC-B. b) If the HARDWARE PART NUMBER is not correct, replace the FCC (PAGEBLOCK 22-11-33/401). (d) Push the LSK next to the PREV MENU prompt. (e) Push the LSK next to the CHANNEL B prompt. 1) Make sure that the HARDWARE PART NUMBER and FCC OPS for channel B are correct. a) If the FCC OPS part number is not correct, load the correct software (TASK 22-11-33-470-823 or TASK 22-11-33-470-820 or TASK 22-11-33-470-824). NOTE: AIRPLANES WITH COLLINS FCCs; If the correct software part number is installed on FCC-A, it may be cross-loaded to FCC-B. b) If the HARDWARE PART NUMBER is not correct, replace the FCC (PAGEBLOCK 22-11-33/401). (f) Push and release the LSK next to the EXIT prompt until you are out of DFCS BITE.

22-11-34-100-801DFCS Mode Control Panel Cleaning ATA 22 · Task 100-801

Task Description

2. DFCS Mode Control Panel Cleaning

A. General

(1) The mode control panel must not be cleaned with the incorrect liquid. The procedure cautions must be obeyed to make sure that there is no damage to the mode control panel.

B. Consumable Materials

C. Location Zones

Zone Area 211 Flight Compartment - Left 212 Flight Compartment - Right

D. Procedure

SUBTASK 22-11-34-420-001 (1) Clean the surface of the MCP: CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE OUTLET HOSE OF COMPRESSED AIR HAS AN AIR IONIZING GUN ATTACHMENT OR AIR IONIZING NOZZLE. YOU CAN DAMAGE THE MCP IF THE AIR IS NOT IONIZED. (a) Use the compressed air or a brush (soft and natural bristle) to remove light dirt and dust from the surface of the MCP . CAUTION DO NOT APPLY THE ISOPROPYL ALCOHOL IN LARGE QUANTITIES. THE LIQUID MAY GET INSIDE A COMPONENT OF THE MCP AND CAUSE DAMAGE. (b) Use the cotton swab with a small quantity of alcohol, B00130 to remove heavy oil and grease from the surface of the MCP . CAUTION DO NOT USE LIQUID CLEANING AGENTS TO CLEAN THE LIQUID CRYSTAL DISPLAY (LCD). THE LIQUID CLEANING AGENTS CAN CAUSE MOISTURE CONTAMINATION IN THE LCD MODULES. (c) Use the lens tissue to remove dust, dirt, oil, and grease from the LCD displays and edgelight panel.

22-11-34-740-801Mode Control Panel Installation Test ATA 22 · Task 740-801

Task Description

2. Mode Control Panel Installation Test

A. General

(1) The installation test makes sure that the mode control panel is installed correctly.

B. References

Reference Title 34-21-00-820-801 Air Data Inertial Reference System - Alignment from the FMC CDU (P/B 201) 34-21-00-820-802 Air Data Inertial Reference System - Alignment from the ISDU (P/B 201)

C. Location Zones

Zone Area 211 Flight Compartment - Left 212 Flight Compartment - Right

D. Installation Test

SUBTASK 22-11-34-860-004 (1) On the captain's main instrument panel (P1), turn the control knob of the AFDS FLOOD lights approximately to the middle position. SUBTASK 22-11-34-740-001 (2) Do the Line Replaceable Unit (LRU) replacement test for the Digital Flight Control System (DFCS) Mode Control Panel (MCP): (a) Prepare for the LRU replacement test: 1) Make sure that the BAT switch on the Pilots' Forward Overhead Panel (P5) is in the ON position. 2) Set the STANDBY POWER switch on the Pilots' Forward Overhead Panel (P5) to the AUTO position. 3) Align the Air Data Inertial Reference System (ADIRS). Do this task: Air Data Inertial Reference System - Alignment from the ISDU, TASK 34-21-00-820-802 or Air Data Inertial Reference System - Alignment from the FMC CDU, TASK 34-21-00-820-801. 4) Make sure that all the instrument switches, on the P5 Forward Overhead Panel, are in the NORMAL position. 5) Make sure that the airplane is in the ground mode. 22-11-34 6) Make sure that the autopilot is disengaged. 7) Make sure that the Inertial Reference System (IRS) ground speed is less than 20 knots or the Flight Management Computer (FMC) ground speed is less than 20 knots. (b) Push the INIT REF key on the Flight Management Computer System (FMCS) Control Display Unit (CDU). (c) Push the Line Select Key (LSK) adjacent to <INDEX. (d) Push the LSK adjacent to MAINT>. (e) Push the LSK adjacent to <DFCS. NOTE: The DFCS self-test will start and will run for a few seconds. (f) Push the LSK adjacent to <LRU REPLACEMENT TESTS. (g) Push the LSK adjacent to <CHANNEL A AND B. (h) Push the LSK adjacent to <MCP . (i) Do the preparation steps as shown on the CDU display. (j) Push the LSK adjacent to <CONTINUE. NOTE: The A/P (Autopilot) disengage aural warning may sound during the test. This warning does not affect performance and test result. Push the captain or first officer autopilot disengage switch to clear the A/P disengage aural warning after the test is completed. (k) Make sure that the test is completed with no failure. NOTE: If a failure occurs, the TEST FAILED indication will show on the CDU display. (l) If a failure occurs, do these steps: 1) Look at the CDU display and make a note of the channel and the LRU that caused the failure. NOTE: Before you replace a defective component, do the Built-In-Test Equipment (BITE) on the system (if it is applicable) and on the FMS interface subsystems that have the defective component. 2) Replace the LRU that had the failure. 3) Do the LRU REPLACEMENT TEST for DFCS MCP again. (m) Make sure that the CDU display shows TEST PASSED. 1) Make sure that the INTERACTIVE TEST PASSED shows on the CDU display at the end of each interactive test. NOTE: Some tests are too fast to see. The tests passed unless TEST FAILED shows on the CDU display. SUBTASK 22-11-34-740-002 (3) Continue the instructions on the CDU display: (a) Push the LSK adjacent to <EXIT when the TEST COMPLETE shows on the CDU display. (b) Do the instructions on the CDU display. NOTE: The EXIT CONFIGURATION steps are at the end of the DFCS BITE test. Make sure to not push the INIT REF key to exit out of the steps. (c) Push the LSK adjacent to <EXIT . 22-11-34 SUBTASK 22-11-34-860-020 (4) Make sure that the autopilot stab trim cutout switch, on the control stand, is set at the NORMAL position after the completion of the DFCS BITE test. Task Description

4. DFCS Mode Control Panel Knobs - Replacement (Figure 203)

A. General

(1) This task includes the steps to replace the left course indicator control knob, right course indicator control knob, speed indicator control knob, heading indicator control knob, or indicator control altitude knob.

B. Location Zones

Zone Area 211 Flight Compartment - Left 212 Flight Compartment - Right

C. Prepare for the Replacement

SUBTASK 22-11-34-040-001 (1) Do this task: DFCS Mode Control Panel - Deactivation, TASK 22-11-34-040-801.

D. DFCS Mode Control Panel Knobs Replacement

SUBTASK 22-11-34-960-001 (1) Replace the left course indicator control knob [1]. (a) Loosen the setscrews [2] on the left course indicator control knob [1]. (b) Remove the left course indicator control knob [1] by pulling on it. (c) Install the new left course indicator control knob [1] onto the indicator shaft. (d) Make sure that there is clearance of 0.03 ±0.01 in. (0.76 ±0.25 mm) between the bottom face of the knob and the top face of the control panel. (e) Install the setscrews [2] in the left course indicator control knob [1]. 1) Tighten the screws to 3.5 in-lb (0.4 N·m) - 4.25 in-lb (0.48 N·m). SUBTASK 22-11-34-960-002 (2) Replace the speed indicator control knob [3]. (a) Loosen the setscrews [4] on the speed indicator control knob [3]. (b) Remove the speed indicator control knob [3] by pulling on it. (c) Install the new speed indicator control knob [3] onto the indicator shaft. (d) Make sure that there is clearance of 0.03 ±0.01 in. (0.76 ±0.25 mm) between the bottom face of the knob and the top face of the control panel. (e) Install the setscrews [4] in the speed indicator control knob [3]. 1) Tighten the screws to 3.5 in-lb (0.4 N·m) - 4.25 in-lb (0.48 N·m). SUBTASK 22-11-34-960-003 (3) Replace the heading indicator control knob [5]. (a) Loosen the setscrews [6] on the heading indicator control knob [5]. (b) Remove the heading indicator control knob [5] by pulling on it. (c) Install the new heading indicator control knob [5] onto the indicator shaft. (d) Make sure that there is clearance of 0.03 ±0.01 in. (0.76 ±0.25 mm) between the bottom face of the knob and the top face of the bank limit knob. (e) Install the setscrews [6] in the heading indicator control knob [5]. 22-11-34 1) Tighten the screws to 3.5 in-lb (0.4 N·m) - 4.25 in-lb (0.48 N·m). SUBTASK 22-11-34-960-004 (4) Replace the altitude indicator control knob [7]. (a) Loosen the setscrews [8] on the altitude indicator control knob [7]. (b) Remove the altitude indicator control knob [7] by pulling on it. (c) Install the new altitude indicator control knob [7] onto the indicator shaft. (d) Make sure that there is clearance of 0.03 ±0.01 in. (0.76 ±0.25 mm) between the bottom face of the knob and the top face of the control panel. (e) Install the setscrews [8] in the altitude indicator control knob [7]. 1) Tighten the screws to 3.5 in-lb (0.4 N·m) - 4.25 in-lb (0.48 N·m). SUBTASK 22-11-34-960-005 (5) Replace the right course indicator control knob [9]. (a) Loosen the setscrews [10] on the right course indicator control knob [9]. (b) Remove the right course indicator control knob [9] by pulling on it. (c) Install the new right course indicator control knob [9] onto the indicator shaft. (d) Make sure that there is clearence of 0.03 ±0.01 in. (0.76 ±0.25 mm) between the bottom face of the knob and the top face of the control panel. (e) Install the setscrew [10] in the right course indicator control knob [9]. 1) Tighten the screws to 3.5 in-lb (0.4 N·m) - 4.25 in-lb (0.48 N·m).

SUBTASK 22-11-37-860-007 (3) Set the left and right IRS select switches on the P5 aft overhead panel to ALIGN or NAV. 22-11-37

H. Installation Test

SUBTASK 22-11-37-740-001 (1) Do the following Digital Flight Control System (DFCS) BITE tests to verify the IFSAU interfaces for correct operation: (a) Do the DFCS BITE CURRENT STATUS AUTOTEST (TASK 22-11-00-740-801). 1) Make sure that the CURRENT STATUS test passes with no failures. Task Description

2. Takeoff/Go-Around Switch Removal (Figure 401)

A. Tools/Equipment

Reference Description STD-3905 Gun - Soldering

B. Consumable Materials

C. Location Zones

Zone Area 211 Flight Compartment - Left 212 Flight Compartment - Right

D. Removal Procedure

SUBTASK 22-11-39-860-001 (1) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name C 5 C01041 AFCS SYS A SNSR EXC AC D 1 C01049 AFCS SYS A WARN LIGHT (BAT) D 2 C01045 AFCS SYS A FCC DC E 1 C00721 AUTOTHROTTLE DC 1 RYR 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020 E 3 C01141 AUTOTHROTTLE DC 2 F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name RYR ALL B 1 C00374 AFCS SYS B WARN LIGHT (BAT) B 3 C01046 AFCS SYS B FCC DC C 2 C01042 AFCS SYS B SNSR EXC AC SUBTASK 22-11-39-860-002 (2) Make sure that the engines are not in operation. 22-11-39 SUBTASK 22-11-39-860-003 (3) Put the thrust lever in a position so that you can get access to the switch [6]. SUBTASK 22-11-39-010-001 (4) Remove the applicable cover [4] or [5] from the left or right thrust lever. (a) Remove the screws [7] from the applicable cover. SUBTASK 22-11-39-020-001 (5) Do these steps to remove the switch [6]: (a) Remove the lacing tape that attaches the TOGA switch wire bundle. (b) Remove the screws [8] which attach the switch holder [3] and the switch [6] to the thrust lever. (c) Remove the hex nut [1], and the lockwasher [2] from the switch [6]. (d) Remove the switch [6] from the switch holder [3]. (e) Remove the heat shrinkable RT-876 sleeve, G01148 or Versafit heat shrink tubing, G51210 from the switch terminals. (f) Use the soldering gun, STD-3905 to melt the solder on the switch terminals to release the wires from the switch [6]. 1) Make a record of the wire positions and the locations of the switch terminals. (g) Remove the switch [6].

A. References

B. Tools/Equipment

Reference Description STD-442 Gun - Heat, 180 deg. F (82 deg. C) Maximum Output T emperature STD-3905 Gun - Soldering

C. Consumable Materials

E. Location Zones

Zone Area 211 Flight Compartment - Left 22-11-39 (Continued) Zone Area 212 Flight Compartment - Right F. TOGA Switch Installation SUBTASK 22-11-39-860-004 (1) Make sure that these circuit breakers are open and have safety tags: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name C 5 C01041 AFCS SYS A SNSR EXC AC D 1 C01049 AFCS SYS A WARN LIGHT (BAT) D 2 C01045 AFCS SYS A FCC DC E 1 C00721 AUTOTHROTTLE DC 1 RYR 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020 E 3 C01141 AUTOTHROTTLE DC 2 F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name RYR ALL B 1 C00374 AFCS SYS B WARN LIGHT (BAT) B 3 C01046 AFCS SYS B FCC DC C 2 C01042 AFCS SYS B SNSR EXC AC SUBTASK 22-11-39-420-001 (2) Do these steps to install the switch [6]: (a) Put the wire for each terminal of the switch [6] through a heat shrinkable RT-876 sleeve, G01148, or Versafit heat shrink tubing, G51210. (b) Use the soldering gun, STD-3905, to solder the wires to the new TOGA switch terminals. (c) Push the heat shrinkable RT-876 sleeve, G01148, or Versafit heat shrink tubing, G51210, on all of the switch terminals. (d) Use the heat 180 deg. F (82 deg. C) maximum output temperature heat gun, STD-442, to blow the hot air on the heat shrinkable RT-876 sleeve, G01148, or Versafit heat shrink tubing, G51210, to make it smaller and tighter. G. Hydraulic Pressure Switch Installation

SUBTASK 22-11-40-420-001 (2) Do these steps to install the hydraulic pressure switch [1]: 22-11-40 (a) Apply a layer of the MCS 352B fluid, D00054, or hydraulic fluid, D00153, to the new packing [2]. (b) Apply a layer of the hydraulic MCS 352B fluid, D00054, or hydraulic fluid, D00153, to the threads of the hydraulic pressure switch [1]. (c) Install the packing [2] on the hydraulic pressure switch [1]. (d) Install the hydraulic pressure switch [1]. (e) Tighten the aileron hydraulic pressure switch [1] to 70 in-lb (7.9 N·m) - 115 in-lb (13.0 N·m). (f) Tighten the elevator hydraulic pressure switch [1] to 70 in-lb (7.9 N·m) - 120 in-lb (13.6 N·m). (g) Install MS20995NC32 lockwire, G01912, on the hydraulic pressure switch [1] per double twist method (TASK 20-10-44-400-801). (h) Examine the connector for corrosion (SWPM 20-60-03). 1) If there is corrosion, refer to SWPM 20-60-03 to correct the problem. (i) Apply the D5026NS or ZC-026 compound, G50171, to the connector (SWPM 20-60-03). (j) Connect the electrical connector to the hydraulic pressure switch [1]. The A/P aileron actuator B and A/P elevator actuator B have interfaces with the Flight Control Computer B (FCC-B) (Channel B). 7) CHANNEL A 8) CHANNEL B 9) CHANNEL A AND B 10) RUN SELECT LIBRARY TESTS 11) 30 ELEV CONTROL or 31 AIL CONTROL NOTE: The 30 ELEV CONTROL is for the A/P elevator actuators and 31 AIL CONTROL is for the A/P aileron actuators. 12) EXECUTE 13) Do the instructions that show on the CDU to complete the test. RYR 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020; AIRPLANES WITH HONEYWELL FCC HARDWARE INSTALLED NOTE: If the test of the library 60.30 (30 ELEVATOR) shows “TEST FAILED” at step S053, but the fail values on the CDU are between the expanded limits (-2.88, -2.10) and the remainder of the test passes, then the full test is a TEST PASS. NOTE: If the system continues to fail with expanded limits, it is necessary to check the friction in the elevator cable system, including all pulleys. Also it is necessary to check the spring force of the springs within the feel of centering (TASK 27-31-64-400-802). B. Location Zones

Zone Area 211 Flight Compartment - Left 212 Flight Compartment - Right

C. Removal Procedure

SUBTASK 22-11-41-860-001 (1) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name C 4 C00456 AFCS SYS A MACH TRIM AC C 5 C01041 AFCS SYS A SNSR EXC AC D 1 C01049 AFCS SYS A WARN LIGHT (BAT) D 2 C01045 AFCS SYS A FCC DC D 3 C01048 AFCS SYS A ENGAGE INTLK D 4 C00457 AFCS SYS A MACH TRIM DC D 5 C01044 AFCS MCP DC 1 F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name B 1 C00374 AFCS SYS B WARN LIGHT (BAT) B 2 C01064 AFCS SYS B MACH TRIM DC 22-11-41 (Continued) F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name B 3 C01046 AFCS SYS B FCC DC B 4 C00716 AFCS SYS B ENGAGE INTLK C 1 C01037 AFCS SYS B MACH TRIM AC C 2 C01042 AFCS SYS B SNSR EXC AC C 3 C01047 AFCS MCP DC 2 SUBTASK 22-11-41-020-001 (2) Do these steps to remove the switch [1]: (a) At the center of the control wheel, remove the screws [4] on the medallion and approach plate [5]. NOTE: The medallion is part of the approach plate. 1) Remove the medallion and approach plate [5]. (b) Use the extraction insertion/extraction tool, COM-3934 to disconnect the eight wires on the autopilot disengage switch side of the wire connectors in the center of the control wheel. (c) Attach one end of the threading wire around the eight wires that connect to the switch [1]. NOTE: For the threading wire, you can use a 30-inch (76.2 centimeters) length of standard wire (No. 18 to 20 gage, without insulation). (d) Remove the screw [3] on the outboard horn of the control wheel. (e) Remove the switch plate [2]. (f) Pull the switch [1] and its eight wires through the control wheel horn slowly until the threading wire shows. NOTE: Pull until approximately 3 inches (76.2 millimeters) of the threading wire comes out of the control wheel horn. Do not remove the threading wire. It is necessary to use this threading wire for the installation. (g) Remove the eight wires from the threading wire.

NOTE: Apply the primer, C00259, on the threads only. (b) Make sure that the threading wire is in the control wheel horn and the two ends of the threading wire show. (c) Attach the end of the threading wire that comes out of the control wheel horn around the eight wires of the switch [1]. (d) Pull the eight wires down through the control wheel horn with the opposite end of the threading wire. (e) Put the switch [1] in its position for installation. 1) Install the switch plate [2] to the control wheel horn with the screw [3]. (f) Remove the threading wire from the eight wires. (g) Use the insertion insertion/extraction tool, COM-3934, to connect the eight wires to the wire connectors in the center of the control wheel. NOTE: There are two equivalent switches you can use for the autopilot disconnect function. The switches have different part numbers and some different wire colors. NOTE: The wires on the 721101-A1 switch are white. The switch wire labels are stamped onto the wires. The wires on the SW43896 switch each have a different color. NOTE: In the AIRPLANE WIRE COLOR column of the table, the second color is for the stripe on the wire. 22-11-41 (h) Use Table 401 for the switch part number 721101-A1 or Table 402 for the switch part number SW43896. Table 401/22-11-41-993-802 Wire Colors for Switch 721101-A1 SWITCH WIRE LABEL AIRPLANE WIRE COLOR BKB BLACK/BLUE BRN BROWN GRN GREEN YEL YELLOW BKG (Not Used) (Not Used) BKY (Not Used) (Not Used) BKA BLACK/GRAY BLU BLUE Table 402/22-11-41-993-803 Wire Colors for Switch SW43896 SWITCH WIRE COLOR AIRPLANE WIRE COLOR BLACK BLACK/BLUE BROWN BROWN GREEN GREEN YELLOW YELLOW GRAY (Not Used) (Not Used) ORANGE (Not Used) (Not Used) WHITE BLACK/GRAY BLUE BLUE (i) Put the wire connectors on top of the terminal block [6]. (j) Install the medallion and approach plate [5] with the screws [4]. SUBTASK 22-11-41-860-003 (3) Remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name C 4 C00456 AFCS SYS A MACH TRIM AC C 5 C01041 AFCS SYS A SNSR EXC AC D 1 C01049 AFCS SYS A WARN LIGHT (BAT) D 3 C01048 AFCS SYS A ENGAGE INTLK D 4 C00457 AFCS SYS A MACH TRIM DC D 5 C01044 AFCS MCP DC 1 F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name B 1 C00374 AFCS SYS B WARN LIGHT (BAT) B 2 C01064 AFCS SYS B MACH TRIM DC 22-11-41 (Continued) F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name B 4 C00716 AFCS SYS B ENGAGE INTLK C 1 C01037 AFCS SYS B MACH TRIM AC C 2 C01042 AFCS SYS B SNSR EXC AC C 3 C01047 AFCS MCP DC 2 SUBTASK 22-11-41-860-017 (4) Remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name D 2 C01045 AFCS SYS A FCC DC F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name B 3 C01046 AFCS SYS B FCC DC SUBTASK 22-11-41-860-004 (5) Do this task: Supply Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-811. SUBTASK 22-11-41-860-005 (6) Make sure that the autopilot stab trim cutout switch, on the control stand, is in the NORMAL position. SUBTASK 22-11-41-860-006 (7) Make sure that the VHF NAV and IRS switches, on the P5 forward overhead panel, are in the NORMAL positions. SUBTASK 22-11-41-860-007 (8) Set the left and right IRS select switches, on the P5 aft overhead panel, to the ALIGN or NAV position. SUBTASK 22-11-41-860-008 WARNING KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT AWAY FROM THE FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES. THE AILERONS, ELEVATORS, RUDDER, FLAPS, SLATS, SPOILERS, STABILIZER, AND NOSE GEAR CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (9) Supply hydraulic power to hydraulic systems A and B, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801.

G. Installation Test

SUBTASK 22-11-41-740-001 (1) Do this manual test: (a) Push the CMD A or CMD B autopilot engage switch on the mode control panel to engage the autopilot. 1) Make sure that the CMD A or CMD B autopilot engage switch light comes on. (b) Push the captain or first officer autopilot disengage switch on the control wheel to disengage the autopilot. 22-11-41 1) Make sure that the A/P warning lights flash. 2) Make sure that the A/P disengage warning sound comes on. 3) Push the captain or first officer autopilot disengage switch again. a) Make sure that the A/P warning lights go off. b) Make sure that there is no A/P disengage warning sound.

H. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 22-11-41-860-009 (1) Remove hydraulic power from hydraulic systems A and B, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805. SUBTASK 22-11-41-860-010 (2) Do this task: Remove Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-812.

22-11-81-710-801Stabilizer Trim Motor Autopilot Test ATA 22 · Task 710-801

Task Description

2. Stabilizer Trim Motor Autopilot Test

A. References

Reference Title 24-22-00-860-811 Supply Electrical Power (P/B 201) 24-22-00-860-812 Remove Electrical Power (P/B 201) 29-11-00-860-801 Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization (P/B 201) 29-11-00-860-805 Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal (P/B 201) 34-21-00-820-801 Air Data Inertial Reference System - Alignment from the FMC CDU (P/B 201) 34-21-00-820-802 Air Data Inertial Reference System - Alignment from the ISDU (P/B 201)

B. Location Zones

Zone Area 211 Flight Compartment - Left 212 Flight Compartment - Right

C. Procedure

SUBTASK 22-11-81-860-001 (1) Do this task: Supply Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-811. SUBTASK 22-11-81-860-006 (2) Set the autopilot stab trim cutout switch, on the control stand, to the NORMAL position. SUBTASK 22-11-81-860-007 (3) Make sure that the VHF NAV and IRS switches, on the P5 forward overhead panel, are in the NORMAL positions. SUBTASK 22-11-81-860-008 (4) Do this task: Air Data Inertial Reference System - Alignment from the ISDU, TASK 34-21-00-820-802 or Air Data Inertial Reference System - Alignment from the FMC CDU, TASK 34-21-00-820-801. SUBTASK 22-11-81-860-002 WARNING KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT AWAY FROM THE FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES. THE AILERONS, ELEVATORS, RUDDER, FLAPS, SLATS, SPOILERS, STABILIZER AND NOSE GEAR CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (5) Supply hydraulic power to hydraulic systems A and B. To supply hydraulic power, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801. SUBTASK 22-11-81-980-001 (6) Set the stabilizer to 5 units of trim. 22-11-81 SUBTASK 22-11-81-860-003 (7) Make sure that the trailing edge flaps are in the UP position. SUBTASK 22-11-81-980-002 (8) Engage the autopilot A in the CWS mode. SUBTASK 22-11-81-980-003 (9) Pull the control column to the aft position approximately 2 inches (51 mm). Release the control column. To prevent a camout of the control column, keep the force on the control column below 15 pounds. NOTE: These conditions can cause the STAB OUT OF TRIM light to come on during the test: 1. Camout of the control column. 2. STAB NOSE UP or STAB NOSE DOWN limit switches are engaged. 3. The Stab Trim Motor is bad and did not operate at the correct rate. SUBTASK 22-11-81-210-001 (10) Make sure that these occur: (a) The stabilizer starts to move. (b) The stabilizer leading edge moves down at a rate of 3 units in 30 to 40 seconds. SUBTASK 22-11-81-980-004 (11) Disengage the autopilot A. SUBTASK 22-11-81-980-005 (12) Set the stabilizer to 5 units of trim. SUBTASK 22-11-81-980-006 (13) Extend the flaps to 5 degrees. SUBTASK 22-11-81-980-007 (14) Engage the autopilot B in the CWS mode. SUBTASK 22-11-81-980-008 (15) Push the control column to the fwd position approximately 2 inches (51 mm). Release the control column. To prevent a camout of the control column, keep the force on the control column below 15 pounds. NOTE: These conditions can cause the STAB OUT OF TRIM light to come on during the test: 1. Camout of the control column. 2. STAB NOSE UP or STAB NOSE DOWN limit switches are engaged. 3. The Stab Trim Motor is bad and did not operate at the correct rate. SUBTASK 22-11-81-210-002 (16) Make sure that these occur: (a) The stabilizer starts to move. (b) The stabilizer leading edge moves up at a rate of 1 unit in 4 to 7 seconds. SUBTASK 22-11-81-980-009 (17) Disengage the autopilot B. SUBTASK 22-11-81-860-010 (18) Set the mode select switches on the inertial reference system (IRS) and mode select unit (MSU) to the OFF position. 22-11-81 SUBTASK 22-11-81-980-010 (19) Set the flaps in the UP position. SUBTASK 22-11-81-860-004 (20) Remove hydraulic power from hydraulic systems A and B. To remove hydraulic power, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805. SUBTASK 22-11-81-860-005 (21) Do this task: Remove Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-812.

SUBTASK 22-11-92-860-012 (1) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name C 4 C00456 AFCS SYS A MACH TRIM AC C 5 C01041 AFCS SYS A SNSR EXC AC D 1 C01049 AFCS SYS A WARN LIGHT (BAT) D 2 C01045 AFCS SYS A FCC DC D 3 C01048 AFCS SYS A ENGAGE INTLK D 4 C00457 AFCS SYS A MACH TRIM DC D 5 C01044 AFCS MCP DC 1 F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name B 1 C00374 AFCS SYS B WARN LIGHT (BAT) B 2 C01064 AFCS SYS B MACH TRIM DC B 3 C01046 AFCS SYS B FCC DC B 4 C00716 AFCS SYS B ENGAGE INTLK C 1 C01037 AFCS SYS B MACH TRIM AC C 2 C01042 AFCS SYS B SNSR EXC AC C 3 C01047 AFCS MCP DC 2 SUBTASK 22-11-92-940-001 (2) Do these steps to prepare for the removal: 22-11-92 (a) To get access to the pitch force transducer [1], open this access door: Number Name/Location 112A Forward Access Door (b) Remove the lockwire from the mass balance weight [4]. (c) Remove the bolts [2] and washers [3] that attach the mass balance weight [4] to the forward quadrant assembly.

D. Pitch Force Transducer Removal

SUBTASK 22-11-92-020-003 (1) Do these steps to remove the pitch force transducer [1]: (a) Disconnect the pitch force transducer connectors. (b) Remove electrical cables from the clamps [5]. (c) Loosen the bolts [16] on the quadrant assembly. 1) Do not remove bolts [16] fully. NOTE: This avoids possible damage to rod-end assembly. (d) Remove the bolt [6], washer [10], and nut [11] from the pitch adjustable rod end [7] of the pitch force transducer [1]. (e) Remove the bolt [15], washer [10], and nut [11] from the pitch force transducer [1] and quadrant assembly. (f) Remove the pitch force transducer [1].

SUBTASK 22-11-92-420-002 (2) Put the pitch force transducer [1] into position on the quadrant assembly. NOTE: The adjustable rod end must point forward on the right quadrant. The adjustable rod end must point aft on the left quadrant. SUBTASK 22-11-92-020-006 (3) Make sure that the bolts [16] are loose. SUBTASK 22-11-92-420-003 (4) Attach electrical cables to the electrical clamps [5]. NOTE: Do not pull the electrical cables tightly. SUBTASK 22-11-92-420-005 (5) Install pitch force transducer [1] to the quadrant assembly with the bolt [15], washer [10], and nut [11]. 22-11-92 SUBTASK 22-11-92-420-004 (6) Connect the pitch force transducer [1] connectors. (a) For the captain's side pitch force transducer [1] (M219), do these steps: 1) Connect the A side pitch force transducer [1] cable to connector D383. 2) Connect the B side pitch force transducer [1] cable to connector D1673. (b) For the first officer's side pitch force transducer [1] (M220), do these steps: 1) Connect the A side pitch force transducer [1] cable to connector D385. 2) Connect the B side pitch force transducer [1] cable to connector D1675. SUBTASK 22-11-92-820-001 (7) Do this task: Pitch Force Transducer Adjustment (DFCS BITE Test), TASK 22-11-92-820-801. NOTE: The installation will be completed in the Adjustment/Test. F. Prepare for the Pitch Force Transducers Adjustment SUBTASK 22-11-92-800-001 (1) Make sure that the cable tension of the elevator control cables are adjusted correctly (TASK 27-31-00-820-801). NOTE: If the cables are not rigged properly then there may be a pitch control wheel steering fault BITE message. SUBTASK 22-11-92-730-003 (2) Do this task: Null Procedure - Mach Trim Actuator, TASK 27-31-00-700-801. SUBTASK 22-11-92-860-001 (3) Do this task: Supply Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-811. G. Pitch Force Transducer Adjustment

SUBTASK 22-11-92-740-001 (1) Make these selections on the Control Display Unit (CDU): (a) Push the INIT REF key on the CDU keyboard. (b) <INDEX (c) MAINT> (d) <DFCS (e) <EXTENDED MAINTENANCE (f) <RIGGING (g) <CWS (h) <CONTINUE (i) Do the instructions shown on the CDU. (j) Push the Line Select Key (LSK) adjacent to <PITCH CWS. (k) Do the instructions shown on the CDU. NOTE: Do not apply force to the control column for tests 55.01, 55.02, and 55.03. The control column must be at neutral for these tests. 22-11-92 SUBTASK 22-11-92-980-001 (2) Do these steps to set the B dimension (Figure 501): NOTE: The B dimension is measured between the center of the upper and lower Gimbal pins on the stabilizer trim jackscrew. To do this, one person must be in the tail of the airplane with a headset and the other person in the flight compartment (a) Make sure that the MAIN STABILIZER TRIM CUTOUT switch, on the control stand, is in the NORMAL position. WARNING STAY AWAY FROM THE STABILIZER TRIM WHEEL ON THE CONTROL STAND IF YOU USE THE STABILIZER TRIM SWITCH ON THE CONTROL WHEEL. THE STABILIZER TRIM SWITCH CAN CAUSE THE STABILIZER TRIM WHEEL TO TURN QUICKLY . INJURY TO PERSONS CAN OCCUR IF YOU TOUCH IT WHEN IT TURNS. (b) Set the B dimension to 39.89 ±0.01 in. (1013.21 ±0.25 mm). NOTE: This B dimension is equivalent to the horizontal stabilizer at 4 units of trim (zero degrees). CAUTION MAKE SURE TO GIVE PROTECTION TO THE WIRE BUNDLES WHEN YOU USE THE TRAMMEL BAR, SPL-1677. THE TRAMMEL BAR HAS SHARP EDGES THAT CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE WIRE BUNDLE INSULATION. (c) Use the trammel trammel bar, SPL-1677, to measure the B dimension. 1) Make sure that the B dimension is 39.89 ±0.01 in. (1013.21 ±0.25 mm). SUBTASK 22-11-92-740-002 (3) Push the LSK adjacent to <CONTINUE to show test 55.02 PITCH CWS SENSOR RIGGING. NOTE: You can use the procedure that follows to adjust the captain's or first officer's pitch force transducer. Test 55.02 is for the captain's pitch force transducer, if it is necessary. After you complete the adjustment procedure for the captain's pitch force transducer, push the LSK adjacent to <CONTINUE on the CDU. The CDU display will show test 55.03. Test 55.03 is for the adjustment of the first officer's pitch force transducer, if it is necessary. SUBTASK 22-11-92-860-003 (4) Insert rig pin E-5, from the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, in the aft quadrant. (a) Make sure that the rig pin E-5 goes through easily and freely. SUBTASK 22-11-92-080-004 (5) Remove the rig pin E-5 from the aft quadrant. SUBTASK 22-11-92-480-002 (6) Install rig pin E-1, from the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, in the left forward quadrant. NOTE: The rig pin E-1 must go through easily and freely. SUBTASK 22-11-92-020-001 (7) If the mass balance weight [4] is installed, do these steps: (a) Remove the lockwire from the mass balance weight [4] (TASK 20-10-44-000-801). (b) Remove the bolts [2], washers [3], and mass balance weight [4] from the elevator forward quadrant assembly. 22-11-92 SUBTASK 22-11-92-020-004 (8) Make sure that the bolt [16] near the side of the adjustable rod end [7] is loose. SUBTASK 22-11-92-020-005 (9) Remove the bolt [6], washer [10], and nut [11] from the adjustable rod end [7] of the applicable pitch force transducer [1]. SUBTASK 22-11-92-020-002 (10) Move the adjustable rod end [7] of the pitch force transducer [1] out of the quadrant assembly attachment point. SUBTASK 22-11-92-970-001 (11) Record the null voltage shown on the CDU. SUBTASK 22-11-92-220-001 (12) Make sure that the null voltage shown on the CDU is less than 0.080 VAC. NOTE: If the null voltage is more than 0.080 VAC, make sure that no external force is applied to the transducer. SUBTASK 22-11-92-020-007 (13) Remove the lockwire from the locknut [8], locknut [18], locktab [17], and adjusting nut [12] on the captain's (or first officer's) pitch force transducer [1]. SUBTASK 22-11-92-020-008 (14) Loosen the locknut [8] so that the adjusting nut [12] can be turned with fingers. SUBTASK 22-11-92-820-002 (15) Adjust the pitch force transducer [1] so the adjustable rod end [7] can be installed. NOTE: For coarse adjustment, turn the rod end. For a fine adjustment, turn the adjusting nut. SUBTASK 22-11-92-211-001 (16) Make sure that the null voltage shown on the CDU is within 0.040 VAC of the value you recorded earlier. SUBTASK 22-11-92-020-009 (17) Remove the bolt [16], washer [14], and nut [13]. NOTE: This bolt is removed as part of the rigging procedure then reinstalled in subsequent operations. SUBTASK 22-11-92-480-003 (18) Install the rig pin E-2 (captain's) or the rig pin E-3 (first officer's) through the hole where the bolt [16] was removed. SUBTASK 22-11-92-210-001 (19) Make sure that the rig pin E-2 (captain's) or the rig pin E-3 (first officer's), from the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, can be freely inserted. SUBTASK 22-11-92-420-001 (20) Do these steps to install the adjustable rod end [7] of the pitch force transducer [1]: (a) Install the bolt [6], washer [10], and nut [11]. (b) Tighten the nut [11] on the adjustable rod end [7]. (c) Tighten the locknut [8] on the adjusting nut [12] for the pitch force transducer [1]. (d) Install MS20995NC20 lockwire, G02166, for the locknut [8], locknut [18], locktab [17], adjusting nut [12] on the pitch force transducer [1] (TASK 20-10-44-400-801). 22-11-92 SUBTASK 22-11-92-080-002 (21) Remove the rig pins E-2 or E-3, from the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, from the quadrant assemblies. SUBTASK 22-11-92-420-006 (22) Install the bolt [16], washer [14], and nut [13]. SUBTASK 22-11-92-420-007 (23) Tighten the nut [13] to 200 ±40 in-lb (22.60 ±4.52 N·m). SUBTASK 22-11-92-420-008 (24) Install the mass balance weight [4] with the bolts [2] and washers [3]. (a) Tighten the bolts [2]. (b) Install the MS20995NC32 lockwire, G50347, on the bolts [2] (TASK 20-10-44-400-801). SUBTASK 22-11-92-080-003 (25) Remove the rig pin E-1, from the rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, from the left forward quadrant. SUBTASK 22-11-92-710-001 (26) Do this check on the pitch force transducer [1]: (a) Move the control columns lightly until the system is in the center. (b) Make sure that the A and B voltages on the CDU display are less than ±0.20 VAC. (c) Make sure that the difference between the A and B voltages is less than ±0.20 VAC. 1) If the voltage is larger than ±0.20 VAC, do a check on the control quadrant and bearings of the structure. 2) If they are satisfactory, do a check of the cable tension for elevator control cables EA and EB (TASK 27-31-00-820-801).

SUBTASK 22-11-92-860-004 WARNING KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT AWAY FROM THE FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES. THE AILERONS, THE ELEVATORS, THE RUDDER, THE FLAPS, THE SLATS, THE SPOILERS, THE STABILIZER AND THE NOSE GEAR CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. (a) Turn the control wheel clockwise 30 degrees. (b) Turn the control wheel counter-clockwise 30 degrees. 22-11-92 (c) Slowly turn the control wheel to the center. NOTE: You can use the torque wrench adapter, SPL-1674, and lock wire to attach the force gauge, COM-1557, to the control wheel on the control column. SUBTASK 22-11-92-730-002 (2) Do the steps shown on the CDU to complete the test: (a) Make sure that the values for the A side and B side are between the limits that show on the CDU display. SUBTASK 22-11-92-080-001 (3) Remove the force gauge, COM-1557, from the control wheels. (a) Remove torque wrench adapter, SPL-1674, and lock wire, if installed.

(h) <PITCH SENS (i) Do the preparation steps as shown on the CDU. (j) <CONTINUE (k) Make sure that the test is completed with no failure. (l) Push the INIT REF key on the CDU keyboard to get out of the BITE. F. A. References

Reference Title 27-21-00-800-802 Pressure from the Rudder Hydraulic Systems A, B, and Standby - Deactivation (P/B 201)

B. Location Zones

Zone Area 211 Flight Compartment - Left 324 Vertical Fin - Rear Spar To Trailing Edge

C. Access Panels

Number Name/Location 324DR Vertical Fin, Trailing Edge Access

D. Prepare for the Removal

SUBTASK 22-23-11-860-007 (1) Do this task: Pressure from the Rudder Hydraulic Systems A, B, and Standby - Deactivation, TASK 27-21-00-800-802. SUBTASK 22-23-11-860-008 (2) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name C 7 C00285 YAW DAMPER AC D 6 C01354 YAW DAMPER 2 DC D 7 C00286 YAW DAMPER 1 DC SUBTASK 22-23-11-010-003 (3) Find this access panel: Number Name/Location 324DR Vertical Fin, Trailing Edge Access (a) Remove the screws [1] and the skin panel [2] on the right side of the vertical fin to get access to the standby rudder Power Control Unit (PCU): 22-23-11

E. Procedure

SUBTASK 22-23-11-020-001 (1) Do these steps to remove the solenoid valve [3]: (a) Remove the bolts [4] that attach the solenoid valve [3] to the standby rudder PCU. (b) Remove the solenoid valve [3]. (c) Remove the gasket plate [9]. 1) If the seals on the gasket plate [9] are in bad condition, discard the gasket plate [9]. (d) Remove and discard the o-ring [7]. (e) Put plugs on the standby rudder PCU ports. SUBTASK 22-23-11-020-002 (2) Do these steps to remove the electrohydraulic servo valve [5]: (a) Remove the bolts [6] that attach the electrohydraulic servo valve [5] to the standby rudder PCU. (b) Remove the electrohydraulic servo valve [5]. (c) Remove the gasket plate [8]. 1) If the seals on the gasket plate [8] are in bad condition, discard the gasket plate [8]. (d) Remove and discard the o-ring [7]. (e) Put plugs on the standby rudder PCU ports.

G. Standby Rudder PCU Solenoid and Electrohydraulic Servo Valves Installation

SUBTASK 22-23-11-020-003 (1) Do these steps to install the solenoid valve [3]: (a) Remove the plugs on the standby rudder PCU ports. (b) Lubricate the o-ring [7] with hydraulic fluid, D00153. (c) Install the new o-ring [7]. 22-23-11 (d) Install the gasket plate [9]. (e) Install the solenoid valve [3]. (f) Lightly coat the threads of the bolts [4] with grease, D50106, BATCO X8401-1 grease, D50105, or BATCO X8401-2 grease, D00571. (g) Install the bolts [4] that attach the solenoid valve [3] to the standby rudder PCU. 1) Tighten the bolts [4] to 50 in-lb (5.6 N·m) - 70 in-lb (7.9 N·m). (h) Apply a fillet seal to the interface between the bolts [4] and solenoid valve [3], do the following steps: 1) Use solvent, B50281, to clean the area and let the area dry. 2) Apply a bead of PR-1440 B-2 sealant, A50527, or PR-1440 B-1/2 sealant, A50387, around the head of each of the bolts [4] and let a sealant cure. 3) Use Akzo Nobel 683-3-2 coating, C00012, or Akzo Nobel 683-3-20 coating, C50238, to apply a top coating on the sealant. (i) Install a MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048, on the bolts [4]. (j) Apply a fillet seal to the interface between the solenoid valve [3] and standby rudder PCU, do the following steps: 1) Use technical grade methyl ethyl ketone, B50046, to clean the area and let the area dry. 2) Apply a bead of sealant, A50419, or sealant, A50110, around the interface between the solenoid valve [3] and gasket plate [9] and between the gasket plate [9] and standby rudder PCU. SUBTASK 22-23-11-020-004 (2) Do these steps to install the electrohydraulic servo valve [5]: (a) Remove the plugs on the standby rudder PCU ports. (b) Lubricate the o-ring [7] with hydraulic fluid, D00153. (c) Install the new o-ring [7]. (d) Install the gasket plate [8]. (e) Install the electrohydraulic servo valve [5]. (f) Lightly coat the threads of the bolts [6] with grease, D50106, BATCO X8401-1 grease, D50105, or BATCO X8401-2 grease, D00571. (g) Install the bolts [6] that attach the electrohydraulic servo valve [5] to the standby rudder PCU. 1) Tighten the bolts [6] to 50 in-lb (5.6 N·m) - 70 in-lb (7.9 N·m). (h) Apply a fillet seal to the interface between the bolts [6] and electrohydraulic servo valve [5], do the following steps: 1) Use solvent, B50281, to clean the area and let the area dry. 2) Apply a bead of PR-1440 B-2 sealant, A50527, or PR-1440 B-1/2 sealant, A50387, around the head of each of the bolts [6] and let a sealant cure. 3) Use Akzo Nobel 683-3-2 coating, C00012, or Akzo Nobel 683-3-20 coating, C50238, to apply a top coating on the sealant. (i) Install a MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048, on the bolts [6]. (j) Apply a fillet seal to the interface between the electrohydraulic servo valve [5] and standby rudder PCU, do the following steps: 22-23-11 1) Use technical grade methyl ethyl ketone, B50046, to clean the area and let the area dry. 2) Apply a bead of sealant, A50419, or sealant, A50110, around the interface between the electrohydraulic servo valve [5] and gasket plate [8] and between the gasket plate [8] and standby rudder PCU.

E. Procedure

SUBTASK 22-23-21-020-001 (1) Do these steps to remove the solenoid valve [4]: (a) Remove the bolts [5 ] that attach the solenoid valve [4] to the main rudder PCU. (b) Remove the solenoid valve [4]. (c) Remove the gasket plate [3]. 1) If the seals on the gasket plate [3] are in bad condition, discard the gasket plate [3]. (d) Remove and discard the o-ring [8]. (e) Put plugs on the main rudder PCU ports to avoid hydraulic fluid contamination. SUBTASK 22-23-21-020-002 (2) Do these steps to remove the electrohydraulic servo valve [6]: (a) Remove the bolts [7] that attach the electrohydraulic servo valve [6] to the main rudder PCU. (b) Remove the electrohydraulic servo valve [6]. (c) Remove the gasket plate [9]. 1) If the seals on the gasket plate [9] are in bad condition, discard the gasket plate [9]. (d) Remove and discard the o-ring [8]. (e) Put plugs on the main rudder PCU ports to avoid hydraulic fluid contamination.
